confirmed.title: Quote transition trigger leaves accepted→sent open to direct table updates, bypassing every revert_quote_status reopen guard
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260706030000_closed_short_booking_closure.sql:103 (current trigger body); supabase/migrations/20260311200000_wave2_audit_fixes.sql:979-992 (origin); supabase/migrations/20260719044958_revert_quote_status_deadlock_retry.sql:117-199 (the guards being bypassed); supabase/migrations/20260206174345_fix_security_and_performance_issues.sql:369-377 (quotes_update RLS)
confirmed.detail: The latest `_enforce_quote_status_transition` (re-emitted 20260706030000, still live per later verbatim reproductions) contains the arm `OR (OLD.status = 'accepted' AND NEW.status = 'sent')` with NO `_is_admin_override()` requirement — it is a plain legal edge for any direct UPDATE. It was added in 20260311200000 as a 'failed order conversion rollback' convenience for an old UI flow; the current QuoteBuilder failure path (src/pages/QuoteBuilder.tsx:2679-2695) only writes after verifying the quote is NOT accepted, so no current code needs this edge. Meanwhile the sanctioned reopen path, `revert_quote_status` (hardened 20260718232157, latest 20260719044958), is admin-only, requires a reason, refuses when a non-cancelled order exists, refuses on delivered/invoiced/paid-commission history (QUOTE_REOPEN_HAS_ORDER_HISTORY), zeroes quote_product_draws, rebuilds planned holds, and writes financial_audit_log. The open trigger edge lets any actor passing quotes_update RLS — an admin OR the owning sales_rep — flip an accepted (converted) quote back to 'sent' via a single PostgREST table update with none of those guards. DB-enforcement gap, not React-only: the DB itself permits the transition.
confirmed.evidence: 20260706030000:100-116: `IF (OLD.status = 'draft' AND NEW.status IN ('sent', 'cancelled')) ... OR (OLD.status = 'accepted' AND NEW.status = 'sent') ... THEN RETURN NEW;` — reached only after `IF _is_admin_override() THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;`, i.e. it allows non-override callers. 20260311200000:979-980: `-- STATE-2: Quote revert transition (accepted -> sent) — Allow accepted -> sent for failed order conversion rollback`. Contrast 20260719044958:139: `IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE quote_id = p_quote_id AND status <> 'cancelled') THEN` and :181 `QUOTE_REOPEN_HAS_ORDER_HISTORY`. quotes_update RLS: `USING (is_admin() OR (is_sales_rep() AND created_by = (select auth.uid())))`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sales rep whose quote was converted (status accepted, active confirmed order, draws fully written) issues `PATCH /rest/v1/quotes?id=eq.<id> {"status":"sent"}` with their own JWT. The trigger allows it. The quote reopens with no admin approval, no reason, no audit row; quote_product_draws stay fully drawn and planned holds are not rebuilt. The rep can then edit/re-send/decline/cancel the quote while its order remains active — quote and order lifecycles permanently diverge, booking accounting (draws vs items) is corrupted, and the admin-only + history-guard policy of harden_quote_reopen_history_guards is void.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED. The latest _enforce_quote_status_transition body (supabase/migrations/20260706030000_closed_short_booking_closure.sql:103, the last migration to touch the function, header attests verbatim-from-live) contains 'OR (OLD.status = ''accepted'' AND NEW.status = ''sent'')' as a plain legal edge reachable by non-admin-override callers (_is_admin_override is a GUC set only inside trusted RPCs — 20260323200000:19-27). quotes_update RLS (20260206174345:369-377, never redefined later) admits admin OR owning sales_rep, and no REVOKE on quotes for authenticated exists. Exhaustive check of all quotes triggers (enforce_quote_accepted_fully_drawn fires only entering accepted at 20260610181612:264; terminal-not-drawn covers only declined/cancelled/expired; release-holds fires only entering the terminal set; row_version trigger only bumps; commission triggers are column-scoped to commission_split) shows nothing blocks accepted→sent or checks for an existing order. The bypassed revert_quote_status guards are exactly as claimed (20260719044958: admin-only INSUFFICIENT_ROLE at :31, non-cancelled-order refusal at :139-141, QUOTE_REOPEN_HAS_ORDER_HISTORY at :181, draw zeroing, hold rebuild, audit log). Not documented in docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor the 2026-08-05 section-04 gauntlet baseline (which contains only the Bulk Order Import finding). Minor correction to the finding's detail: src/pages/QuoteBuilder.tsx:2686 still performs a direct quotes status update to 'sent' in the failed-convert rollback (pre-checked not-accepted, but a race window remains), so the edge has a residual consumer — the fix cannot simply delete the arm; it should require admin override or an order-existence guard on the edge. Severity HIGH stands: authenticated insider via direct PostgREST call silently reopens a converted quote with draws intact and an active order, corrupting booking accounting and voiding the hardened admin-only reopen policy, on a path the project requires the DB itself to enforce.

confirmed.title: restore_quote_version reopens terminal/accepted quotes to 'revised' for sales reps, bypassing the reopen history guards entirely
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260703130000_layer2_channel_separation_reserve_fixes.sql:239-252 (impl, via awk-relative numbering inside the restore_quote_version body; the status write and admin-override bracket); supabase/migrations/20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql:1123-1245 (current wrapper — adds ownership/row-version only)
confirmed.detail: `restore_quote_version`'s implementation deliberately brackets its status write with `app.admin_override` so, per its own comment, 'the enforcer permits restore->revised from any source state (accepted/declined/etc.)'. Its role gate is `role IN ('admin','sales_rep')` (owning rep allowed by the 20260730235031 wrapper). It performs NO reopen-history check: no active-order check, no delivered/invoiced/paid-commission history check, no reason parameter, no draw-ledger zeroing, and no planned-hold rebuild — the exact protections 20260718232157_harden_quote_reopen_history_guards added to `revert_quote_status` (which is admin-only). The only guard is BOOKING_OVERDRAWN (restored content may not fall below drawn quantities), which a converted quote passes trivially by restoring equal content. The 2026-07-22 reuse-guard migration (20260722172533:79-81) explicitly documents that 'terminal quotes... are revivable via revert_quote_status / restore_quote_version', but only the name-reuse guard was widened — the order-history guard never was. The 2026-07-30 wrapper rewrite was an opportunity to add a status gate and did not.
confirmed.evidence: 20260703130000 impl: `-- Restore quote-level fields. Bracket the status write with the admin override so the enforcer permits restore->revised from any source state (accepted/declined/etc.). PERFORM set_config('app.admin_override', 'true', true); UPDATE quotes SET ... status = 'revised', updated_at = now() WHERE id = p_quote_id;` Role gate: `AND role IN ('admin', 'sales_rep')`. Wrapper 20260730235031:1158-1180 adds only INSUFFICIENT_ROLE / NOT_QUOTE_OWNER / QUOTE_STALE_WRITE checks — no status or order-history condition anywhere between :1130 and the `_restore_quote_version_owner_impl` call at :1232.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sales rep opens the version history of their own accepted (converted, active order) or cancelled/expired/declined quote and calls restore_quote_version with the current row_version. The quote flips to 'revised' — editable and re-sendable — while its order stays active; for a formerly planned booking whose terminal transition released its holds, the reopened booking now sits open with NO inventory holds (restore does not call create_planned_holds, unlike revert_quote_status), silently un-reserving committed inventory. All admin-only/reason/audit requirements of the reopen policy are skipped.

verdict.reason: Core claim CONFIRMED against source: the restore_quote_version impl (20260703130000:~240-253) brackets its unconditional status='revised' write with app.admin_override, _is_admin_override() (20260323200000:19-26) checks only the GUC with no role verification so _enforce_quote_status_transition (20260706030000:81) is bypassed for sales_rep callers; the 20260730235031 wrapper (1130-1245) adds only owner/row-version/idempotency checks with no status or order-history gate and grants EXECUTE to authenticated; revert_quote_status (20260718232157) is admin-only+reason+history-guarded while restore has none of that; no later migration adds a guard (latest touch is 20260730235031); not documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md or the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline (both grepped clean). HOWEVER two material parts of the failure scenario are factually wrong, so severity drops: (1) the hold-loss claim is false — the impl tail calls _sync_quote_job_reservations (20260710120000:269) which calls _sync_planned_holds (20260702171000:46-50), rebuilding crop_program holds for the now-'revised' planned quote at booked−drawn, so inventory is NOT silently un-reserved; (2) no duplicate-order risk — convert_quote_to_order records the full booking in quote_product_draws at conversion (20260702172500:181-184) and its status-independent draws-guard returns 'already_converted'/raises BOOKING_PARTIALLY_DRAWN on a reopened converted quote, and restore's BOOKING_OVERDRAWN guard keeps booked≥drawn; (3) the UI never exposes restore outside draft/revised (QuoteBuilder.tsx:445 canEdit=['draft','revised']), so exploitation requires a direct authenticated RPC call, not the described version-history UI flow. What remains is a real DB-level authorization/lifecycle asymmetry (sales rep can reopen accepted/terminal quotes to editable 'revised' via API, skipping the admin-only reason-and-history-guarded reopen path) — confirmed, but MED not HIGH.

confirmed.title: Deliveries can be walked scheduled→in_progress→completed by direct table UPDATE, skipping all complete_delivery effects (inventory, order rollup)
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260228300000_critical_prelaunch_fixes.sql:394-415 (trigger arms, unchanged since — 20260319000000 only set search_path); supabase/migrations/20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:83-93 (del_update RLS); supabase/migrations/20260526151856_execute_full_codebase_ultra_review.sql:1513-1533 (signature guard); supabase/migrations/20260716120104_gauntlet_access_boundaries.sql:114-262 (the bypassed effects)
confirmed.detail: `_enforce_delivery_status_transition` allows scheduled→in_progress and in_progress→completed as plain legal edges — no `_is_admin_override()` needed — and deliveries never received the direct-write closure invoices got: there is no `REVOKE UPDATE ON public.deliveries` anywhere in migrations (checked; the only lifecycle-table UPDATE revoke is invoices, 20260719093000), and no delivery counterpart to `guard_order_delivered_activity_cancel` (which forces orders' terminal transitions through RPCs with the message 'USE_RPC'). del_update RLS admits admin, any sales_rep (no ownership scoping), and the assigned driver when the row is in_progress/completed. The only extra hurdle is `guard_completed_delivery_signature`, satisfied by any non-empty `signed_by` string. So a direct UPDATE `{status:'completed', signed_by:'x'}` on an in_progress delivery succeeds while skipping everything complete_delivery does: inventory deduction (or negative-stock warning), delivery_items/order_items quantity_delivered updates, orders fulfilled/partially_fulfilled rollup, delivery_remainders creation, closed-period warning, auto-invoice patching, activity/audit. The same applies to direct scheduled→cancelled by a sales_rep, skipping cancel_delivery's prebook release, remainder handling, commission-batch freeze check, and invoice auto-cancel. Business invariant enforcement is RPC-only with the raw table lane still open — the exact class the C3 triggers were built to stop, but the trigger validates only the edge, not the effects.
confirmed.evidence: 20260228300000:402-406: `IF (OLD.status = 'scheduled' AND NEW.status IN ('in_progress', 'cancelled')) OR (OLD.status = 'in_progress' AND NEW.status IN ('completed', 'cancelled')) THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;` (after the override early-return, i.e. allowed WITHOUT override). 20260511060000:83-93 del_update: `USING ((is_admin() OR is_sales_rep() OR ((assigned_driver = (SELECT auth.uid())) AND (status = ANY (ARRAY['in_progress'::text, 'completed'::text])))))` with matching WITH CHECK. Signature guard: `IF NEW.status = 'completed' AND NULLIF(btrim(COALESCE(NEW.signed_by, '')), '') IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'SIGNATURE_REQUIRED';`. Grep for `REVOKE.*deliveries` returns no table-privilege revoke.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sales rep (any rep — no ownership scoping) or the assigned driver updates an in_progress delivery to completed via PostgREST with signed_by='x'. The delivery reads as completed; no stock leaves inventory, order_items.quantity_delivered stays 0, the order stays confirmed. Net Position now overstates commitments as still-prebooked while ops believes product shipped; a later cancel_delivery on it 'restores' nothing but still regresses/cancels invoices; billing per-delivery flows (create_invoice_for_unbilled_delivery requires delivered quantities) refuse, leaving a completed delivery that can never be billed.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED. Every cited mechanism checks out against current migrations: (1) _enforce_delivery_status_transition (20260228300000:394-415) permits scheduled→in_progress, in_progress→completed, and →cancelled as plain edges without _is_admin_override(); the only later touch is 20260319000000:24 (search_path only) — never tightened to require RPC context. (2) del_update RLS (20260511060000:83-93, last definition) admits admin, ANY sales_rep with no ownership scoping, and the assigned driver while in_progress/completed, with matching WITH CHECK. (3) No REVOKE/GRANT targeting TABLE public.deliveries exists in any migration — the only lifecycle-table UPDATE revoke is invoices (20260719093000:59), and no deliveries counterpart to the orders ORDER_TERMINAL_TRANSITION_USE_RPC guard (20260721014858:1412) exists anywhere. (4) The remaining triggers do not close the lane: guard_completed_delivery_signature (20260526151856:1513-1533) only requires non-empty signed_by; enforce_delivery_accounting_period (latest 20260716183442) only rejects closed-period dates, so open-period completion passes; trg_delivery_status_change (20260210000000:447-474) merely logs to activity_feed. So a direct PostgREST UPDATE {status:'completed', signed_by:'x'} on an in_progress delivery by any sales_rep or the assigned driver succeeds while skipping complete_delivery's inventory deduction, quantity_delivered updates, order rollup, remainders, and invoice patching — checked the migrations; the DB does not enforce this, not merely "not found". Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md or the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline (that section's finding is the Bulk Order Import frontend bypass); the 2026-07-22 section-04 refresh called direct adjunct writes "trigger/RLS bounded" but evaluated only the frontend's actual calls and recorded no accepted-risk decision for this lane. One minor overstatement: activity is not fully skipped — trg_delivery_status_change writes a generic activity_feed row on the status change — but the substantive effects (inventory, rollup, remainders, billing) are genuinely skipped. Exploitation requires an authenticated insider or buggy code issuing a raw table UPDATE, which is exactly the threat model the project already closed for invoices (REVOKE UPDATE), orders (USE_RPC guard), and quote children (20260730235031); HIGH is consistent with how those were rated.

confirmed.title: Order forward-fulfillment edges (confirmed→partially_fulfilled/fulfilled) are open to direct admin updates with no delivery lineage
confirmed.detail: `guard_order_delivered_activity_cancel` (2026-07-21) closed the direct lane for cancelled/voided/soft-delete ('ORDER_TERMINAL_TRANSITION_USE_RPC'), but the forward edges in `_enforce_order_status_transition` — confirmed→partially_fulfilled, confirmed→fulfilled, partially_fulfilled→fulfilled — remain plain legal edges requiring no override. orders_update RLS is admin-only, so this is an admin-JWT lane, but it produces a structurally impossible state with zero RPC effects: an order marked fulfilled whose order_items all have quantity_delivered=0 and quantity_remaining>0, whose prebooked inventory is never released or deducted, with no delivery, no delivered-quantity rollup, and no audit. Once 'fulfilled', create_delivery_with_items refuses the order (ORDER_NOT_SCHEDULABLE requires confirmed/partially_fulfilled), so the real fulfillment can never be recorded; the prebook is stuck. This is precisely the impossible-fulfillment-state class the Section 4 bulk-import fix closed for the INSERT path, still open on the UPDATE path.
confirmed.evidence: 20260228300000:378-380: `IF (OLD.status = 'confirmed' AND NEW.status IN ('partially_fulfilled', 'fulfilled', 'cancelled')) OR (OLD.status = 'partially_fulfilled' AND NEW.status IN ('fulfilled', 'cancelled')) THEN RETURN NEW;` (no override required). 20260721014858:1404-1408 guards only: `IF NEW.status IN ('cancelled', 'voided') AND OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status AND NOT public._is_admin_override() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'ORDER_TERMINAL_TRANSITION_USE_RPC...'`. orders_update: `USING (is_admin()) WITH CHECK (is_admin())`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An admin (or any tooling holding an admin JWT) updates orders.status from 'confirmed' to 'fulfilled' directly. The order shows fulfilled with all items undelivered; inventory quantity_prebooked keeps the units reserved forever; delivery scheduling for the order is now impossible (ORDER_NOT_SCHEDULABLE); commissions/invoices built on 'fulfilled' semantics see a fulfillment that never happened.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED against current source. Every cited mechanism checks out: (1) supabase/migrations/20260228300000_critical_prelaunch_fixes.sql:377-381 lists confirmed→partially_fulfilled/fulfilled and partially_fulfilled→fulfilled as plain "Valid transitions" returning NEW with no _is_admin_override() requirement, and no later migration redefines _enforce_order_status_transition (only 20260319000000:27 alters its search_path; grep for CREATE OR REPLACE of that function matches only the original file). (2) 20260721014858:1403-1408 guard_order_delivered_activity_cancel blocks only NEW.status IN ('cancelled','voided') plus soft-delete — forward edges pass untouched; it is the only migration defining that guard. (3) orders_update RLS is USING(is_admin()) WITH CHECK(is_admin()) at 20260206174345:469-470, and no migration revokes table-level UPDATE on orders from authenticated (grep for REVOKE on orders found none), so an admin JWT can PATCH orders.status directly via PostgREST. (4) The latest create_delivery_with_items definition (20260518010000, no later redefinition) raises ORDER_NOT_SCHEDULABLE at :104-106 for any status other than confirmed/partially_fulfilled, so a bogus 'fulfilled' order can never receive its real delivery. (5) No recovery path exists: void_order (latest, 20260616142001) requires status='fulfilled' but restores inventory only for order_items with quantity_delivered > 0 (:132-137) and syncs holds only for booking_draw quotes (:126), so a zero-delivery fulfilled order voids with its prebooked reservation still stuck. (6) The frontend confirms this is not app-reachable — src/pages/OrderDetail.tsx:624-628 deliberately excludes fulfilled targets from manual status change ("partially_fulfilled/fulfilled happen via delivery RPCs, not manual update") — matching the finding's characterization as an admin-JWT/tooling lane. (7) Not in either baseline: docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md and the 2026-08-05 section-04 refresh contain no mention of enforce_order_status_transition forward edges or direct-UPDATE fulfillment; the section-04 doc covers only the bulk-import INSERT-path impossible-fulfillment fix (20260805211951 forces status='confirmed' at :68), exactly as the finding states. One minor overstatement, not severity-affecting: "no audit" is wrong — trg_order_status_change (20260210000000:416-443, AFTER UPDATE) writes an activity_feed row for any status change, including this one; there is however no RPC-level cascade (inventory/commission/delivery effects) as claimed. Severity MED is correct: admin-only, not UI-reachable, requires deliberate direct API use, but yields an unreconcilable fulfillment/inventory state with no in-app recovery.

confirmed.title: Quote soft delete has no DB guard: deleting a planned booking leaks its active inventory holds permanently; any-status quotes deletable via API
confirmed.location: src/pages/Quotes.tsx:32,323,376-417 (React-only DELETABLE + draws-only check); supabase/migrations/20260312200000_business_logic_audit_fixes.sql:63-67 (hold release fires on UPDATE OF status only); supabase/migrations/20260302200000_business_logic_enhancements.sql (release_expired_quote_holds covers status declined/expired only); supabase/migrations/20260721014858_20260721010000_govern_invoice_order_money_lifecycle.sql:1396-1403 (orders got a soft-delete guard; quotes did not)
confirmed.detail: Quotes are soft-deleted by a raw `.update({ deleted_at })` under quotes_update RLS. Checked the full trigger inventory on quotes (enforce_quote_status_transition, trg_release_holds_on_quote_status, trg_enforce_quote_terminal_not_drawn, validate_quote_commission_splits, row_version, recipient-id stamp): none fires on or guards deleted_at — this is an absence claim from the migration set, stated as 'I found no guard', and the UI's own comment concedes the mechanism ('deletion changes no status, so the hold-release trigger never fires'). The UI mitigation checks ONLY quote_product_draws/job_product_draws (draw ledgers) — not inventory_holds. A planned booking in 'sent' with zero draws but active planned holds (created by create_planned_holds, released only on status transition or conversion) passes DELETABLE=['draft','sent','revised'], is selectable, and soft-deletes with its holds still is_active=true. The nightly `release_expired_quote_holds` cron releases holds only for quotes whose STATUS is declined/expired, so the leaked holds are never reclaimed by any code path. Separately, DELETABLE and the drawn-check are React-only: via PostgREST an owning rep can soft-delete a quote in ANY status including accepted (converted), while orders received a DB-side ORDER_MUST_BE_TERMINAL_BEFORE_DELETE guard for the identical operation.
confirmed.evidence: Quotes.tsx:380-383: `// Open bookings with partial draw-downs must not be soft-deleted: deletion changes no status, so the hold-release trigger never fires — the booking's reserved inventory would stay held on a hidden quote.` (the check below it queries only quote_product_draws and job_product_draws). Trigger: `CREATE TRIGGER trg_release_holds_on_quote_status AFTER UPDATE OF status ON quotes`. Cron body: `UPDATE inventory_holds ih SET is_active = false ... WHERE ih.source_id = q.id AND ih.is_active = true AND q.status IN ('declined', 'expired');`. Orders contrast (20260721014858): `IF OLD.deleted_at IS NULL AND NEW.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND OLD.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'voided') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'ORDER_MUST_BE_TERMINAL_BEFORE_DELETE';`
confirmed.failure_scenario: Office staff bulk-select a planned 'sent' booking that has active planned holds but no draws yet and hit Delete. The quote disappears from every list; its inventory_holds rows stay active forever, so Net Position permanently under-reports available stock by the booked quantity with no visible owner. No sweep or cron reclaims them. Alternatively, a rep API-deletes their accepted quote, orphaning the live order's quote provenance.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED. Every element verified against current source: (1) Quotes.tsx:32/387-411 soft-deletes via raw .update({deleted_at}) with a React-only draws check that never queries inventory_holds; (2) exhaustive migration search confirms all six quote triggers fire only on UPDATE OF status/commission_split (the row_version bump trigger fires on all updates but guards nothing) — no DB mechanism fires on quotes.deleted_at, verified as a checked absence, not a failure to find; (3) the orders contrast is exact: 20260721014858:1404-1422 added ORDER_MUST_BE_TERMINAL_BEFORE_DELETE on 'BEFORE UPDATE OF status, deleted_at ON public.orders' while quotes got nothing; (4) no reclaim path: release_expired_quote_holds (20260302200000:1524-1529, never redefined) covers only status declined/expired, auto_expire_quotes (20260610191550:46) filters deleted_at IS NULL, _sync_planned_holds (20260702171000:42-44) early-returns on deleted quotes; (5) quotes_update RLS (20260206174345:369-377) has no status restriction and UPDATE on quotes was never revoked, so any-status API soft-delete including accepted is real; (6) not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline (which covers only Bulk Order Import). One overstatement that does not refute: "permanently under-reports Net Position" is too strong for dated holds — Net Position readers filter expires_at >= CURRENT_DATE and planned holds carry expires_at = needed_by_date + 14 days, so dated leaked holds stop distorting availability ~2 weeks past needed-by; holds with NULL needed_by_date (NULL expires_at) do distort forever, and the is_active rows are never reclaimed in any case. HIGH stands: an inventory invariant enforced only in React (contra the CRX hard rule), reachable through the normal bulk-delete UI on the normal pre-conversion state of a planned booking, with a weeks-to-permanent availability distortion and an ungated any-status API deletion path.

confirmed.title: cancel_delivery reverses a completed delivery without flagging 'paid' or 'overdue' invoices (only 'posted' is flagged)
confirmed.detail: When cancel_delivery reverses a completed/in_progress delivery (restoring inventory and decrementing order_items.quantity_delivered), its invoice pass selects only status IN ('draft','posted','unposted'): drafts/unposted are cancelled, posted triggers an admin 'Posted Invoice Needs Review' notification. Invoices in 'paid' or 'overdue' — both valid statuses per invoices_status_check and both reachable for a completed delivery's invoice — match nothing: no cancellation, no flag, no notification. The goods reversal proceeds silently while a paid invoice for those goods stands. The DB does not enforce (checked this function body and found no other pass over paid/overdue); this is a coverage hole in the enforcement that exists.
confirmed.evidence: `FOR v_invoice IN SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE order_id = v_delivery.order_id AND status IN ('draft', 'posted', 'unposted') AND deleted_at IS NULL LOOP IF v_invoice.status IN ('draft', 'unposted') THEN ... ELSIF v_invoice.status = 'posted' THEN [admin notification] END IF; END LOOP;` — invoices.status CHECK per .claude/schema-registry.json: ['draft','unposted','posted','paid','overdue','voided','cancelled'].
confirmed.failure_scenario: Customer pays the invoice for a completed delivery (invoice → 'paid'). A sales rep later cancels that delivery (allowed — see the role-asymmetry finding). Inventory returns to stock, quantity_delivered is rolled back, the order regresses to confirmed/partially_fulfilled — and nobody is notified that a PAID invoice now bills goods the system says were never delivered. AR and fulfillment silently diverge until a manual reconciliation.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED. The quoted invoice loop is accurate, and the gap survives into the CURRENT cancel_delivery definition (20260706070000_complete_delivery_per_delivery_billing.sql:694): `status IN ('draft','posted','unposted')` with drafts/unposted cancelled and only 'posted' notified; 'paid' and 'overdue' (both valid per invoices_status_check in .claude/schema-registry.json:1915-1919) match nothing. I read the full current function body — no other pass over invoices exists (checked, absent). The RPC permits cancelling 'completed' deliveries (:589) for role admin OR sales_rep (:590), so the paid-invoice scenario is reachable at the DB enforcement layer. Not documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md or the 2026-08-05 section-04 gauntlet baseline (whose only finding is the Bulk Order Import bypass). One correction to the reviewer's framing: the cited location (20260620130000) is superseded, and the UI blocks cancel on completed deliveries (DeliveryDetail.tsx:190 canCancel excludes 'completed', routing to admin-only void_delivery) — but void_delivery has the identical hole (20260706070000:899-914 cancels only 'draft', flags only 'posted'), the in_progress cancel path is UI-reachable by sales reps and runs the same goods reversal with the same gap for order-level paid/overdue invoices, and 'overdue' invoices miss even the posted-invoice admin notification everywhere. MED severity is appropriate given the partial UI mitigation on the completed path.

confirmed.title: Completed-delivery reversal role asymmetry: void_delivery is admin-only with mandatory reason, but cancel_delivery lets any sales_rep reverse a completed delivery
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260620130000_commission_batch_freeze_guard.sql:673-674 (cancel accepts completed for admin|sales_rep); supabase/migrations/20260716120104_gauntlet_access_boundaries.sql:551-557,577 (void requires admin + reason, completed only)
confirmed.detail: void_delivery enforces 'Admin access required to void a completed delivery' plus a mandatory reason and writes financial_audit_log. cancel_delivery accepts `status IN ('scheduled','in_progress','completed')` and gates on `role IN ('admin','sales_rep')` — so a sales rep reverses a completed delivery (full inventory restore + order_items rollback + order status regression) through the cancel lane, making the admin-only void gate advisory. cancel_delivery also writes no financial_audit_log for the reversal itself (only the quick-delivery auto-cancel branch does). confirmed.title: Jobs: sales_rep direct-update lane allows completed→invoiced with no invoice, permanently stranding the job unbillable
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260620150000_job_cancel_gate.sql:27-44 (trigger arms); supabase/migrations/20260430180000_field_app_workflow_phase5.sql:29-32 (jobs_update RLS: admin|sales_rep); supabase/migrations/20260625190000_guard_billed_job_immutability.sql:87 (immutability keys off OLD.status only)
confirmed.detail: `_enforce_job_status_transition` allows completed→invoiced (and in_progress→completed) as plain legal edges without override, and jobs_update RLS admits any admin or sales_rep. 'invoiced' is supposed to mean transfer_job_to_invoice ran (invoice + commissions + machine-fee records created). A direct `.update({status:'invoiced'})` on a completed job creates the status with none of those artifacts. The billed-job immutability guard then locks the job (OLD.status IN ('invoiced','cancelled') blocks non-admin edits), and the revival path (void_invoice returns an invoiced job to completed) requires an invoice that does not exist — so the job is stuck 'invoiced', excluded from billing pickers, with no invoice and no commissions. The in_progress→completed direct edge likewise skips complete_job's applied-info requirements and auto-draft/notification logic (the #107/#117 activity rows fire only inside complete_job). JobDetail's own cancel path already writes status directly (src/pages/JobDetail.tsx:2478-2485), demonstrating the lane is live; cancel specifically is trigger-covered for holds (_trg_release_job_holds_on_lifecycle) but the forward edges have no effect-triggers at all.
confirmed.evidence: 20260620150000: `IF (OLD.status = 'scheduled' AND NEW.status = 'in_progress') OR (OLD.status = 'in_progress' AND NEW.status = 'completed') OR (OLD.status = 'completed' AND NEW.status = 'invoiced') THEN RETURN NEW;` (after the override check — i.e. open to direct writers). jobs_update: `USING (is_admin() OR is_sales_rep()) WITH CHECK (is_admin() OR is_sales_rep())`. Immutability guard: `IF OLD.status NOT IN ('invoiced', 'cancelled') THEN` (returns early — never inspects whether an invoice exists when ENTERING 'invoiced').
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rep updates a completed spray job's status to 'invoiced' directly (stale tab, script, or misunderstanding). No invoice or commissions exist. The job now reads as billed, drops out of the billing queue, and its splits never mint commissions; the immutability guard blocks correction by non-admins, and void_invoice cannot revive it because there is nothing to void. Revenue for the application is silently never billed.

verdict.reason: Confirmed against current source. (1) 20260620150000_job_cancel_gate.sql:37-42 is the latest _enforce_job_status_transition body (no later migration replaces it) and allows completed→invoiced and in_progress→completed as plain edges with no invoice-existence or admin check. (2) jobs_update RLS (20260430180000:29-32, never redefined later) admits any admin or sales_rep. (3) The current immutability guard (20260629120000, superseding 20260625190000) gates only on OLD.status IN ('invoiced','cancelled') and never validates invoice existence on ENTRY to 'invoiced'; searched all migrations — no CHECK constraint, trigger, or recovery RPC ties status='invoiced' to invoice_id, and the transition enforcer blocks invoiced→completed even for admins (only the _is_admin_override SET LOCAL hatch passes, reachable only inside SECURITY DEFINER RPCs like transfer_invoice_to_job, which requires an existing invoice). So a phantom-invoiced job is unrecoverable from the app, admin included. (4) The direct-write lane is live: JobDetail.tsx ~2473-2495 does raw .update({status:'cancelled'}), and the project's own guard migrations treat non-admin raw REST/psql writes as a proven threat model. (5) Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md (§1b is the distinct, resolved commission name-reuse-on-revival issue) and the 2026-08-05 gauntlet section-04 baseline contains no job content. MED severity stands: no UI path writes status='invoiced' directly, but the consequence is silently unbilled revenue plus a job locked beyond app-level repair.

confirmed.title: save_quote allows full content rewrite of a quote in ANY status (sent, accepted, cancelled, expired, closed_*) as long as status is unchanged — edit lock is React-only
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql:241-248 (transition check only fires when status changes), :269 (unconditional DELETE FROM quote_sections), :478-506 (unconditional totals/header rewrite); src/pages/QuoteBuilder.tsx:445 (canEdit = ['draft','revised'] — the only edit gate)
confirmed.detail: save_quote's lifecycle validation runs only `IF v_status IS DISTINCT FROM v_old_status`. When the caller sends the current status back, no state check of any kind runs: sections are deleted and re-inserted, item prices/quantities rewritten, and totals recalculated, for a quote in any status — including sent (customer-visible; the 'revised' state exists precisely to mark post-send edits), accepted (converted), and every terminal status (cancelled/declined/expired/closed_by_application/closed_short). The BOOKING_OVERDRAWN guard only prevents shrinking below drawn quantities; growing lines or changing prices on an accepted/terminal quote passes. The UI's canEdit=['draft','revised'] is the only thing preventing this — classic React-only enforcement of a business invariant. Caller must be admin or the owning rep and supply the current row_version, both of which the legitimate UI session has. Order money is snapshotted at conversion so the direct blast radius is quote/booking reporting, drawn-guard baselines, and _sync_quote_job_reservations re-syncs on quotes whose lifecycle says they are closed.
confirmed.evidence: `IF v_status IS DISTINCT FROM v_old_status THEN IF NOT (v_allowed_transitions->v_old_status IS NOT NULL AND v_allowed_transitions->v_old_status ? v_status) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid status transition: % -> %'...` — there is no ELSE branch and no separate `v_old_status IN (...)` editability check anywhere in the function; the very next unconditional statements are `v_quote_id := p_quote_id; DELETE FROM quote_sections WHERE quote_id = v_quote_id;`. UI: `const canEdit = ['draft', 'revised'].includes(currentStatus);`
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rep calls save_quote on their own 'sent' quote with status:'sent' and changed prices — the customer-presented quote silently changes without ever passing through 'revised'. Or on a 'cancelled'/'closed_short' booking, the rep rewrites items; _sync_quote_job_reservations re-runs against a closed booking and reported totals for a terminal quote change after the fact, corrupting the terminal snapshot the close decision was based on.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED against current source. 20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql is the latest save_quote definition (no later migration redefines it). Lifecycle validation at :241-248 runs only when v_status IS DISTINCT FROM v_old_status; I read the entire function body (:86-547) and there is no status-based editability check anywhere — the DB does not enforce it (verified absence, not merely not-found). :269 DELETE FROM quote_sections and the :478-506 header/totals UPDATE are unconditional; BOOKING_OVERDRAWN (:430-464) only blocks shrinking below drawn quantities, so price changes and line growth on sent/accepted/terminal quotes pass. No trigger enforces quote immutability by status (full CREATE TRIGGER sweep; trg_release_holds_on_quote_status fires only on status change). The only gate is QuoteBuilder.tsx:445 canEdit=['draft','revised'] — React-only, exactly as claimed. The same migration removed direct browser writes on quote_sections/quote_items (KNOWN_ISSUES.md:216), making save_quote the sole writer and this the remaining server-side gap. Scenario is feasible: EXECUTE granted to authenticated (:1279), owning rep passes ownership/actor/row_version checks. Not documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md, the 2026-08-05 section-04 refresh (bulk-import-focused), earlier section-04 docs, or the workflow-review findings. One imprecision that does not refute: on terminal quotes _sync_quote_job_reservations (20260710120000:148-155) sets v_planned_open=false and will not re-draw a closed booking — its unconditional effect there is deleting job holds/non-consumed draws, not re-drawing. Severity MED is correct: requires a deliberate direct RPC call by an authorized admin/owning rep and order money is snapshotted at conversion, but it silently bypasses the sent→revised versioning workflow, can mutate accepted-quote holds, and corrupts terminal-quote snapshots/reporting.

confirmed.title: Lifecycle tables accept arbitrary creation status on direct INSERT — only invoices have a draft-on-insert trigger
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260302200000_business_logic_enhancements.sql:30-48 (invoices-only enforce_invoice_draft_on_insert); supabase/migrations/20260228300000_critical_prelaunch_fixes.sql:390,413,463,491 (all transition triggers are BEFORE UPDATE only); supabase/migrations/20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:96-99 (del_insert: admin OR sales_rep); supabase/migrations/20260206174345_fix_security_and_performance_issues.sql:363-367 (quotes_insert: admin or rep)
confirmed.detail: Every status-transition trigger is BEFORE UPDATE OF status; INSERTs are validated only by the CHECK constraint (value membership), not by any born-state rule. Invoices got a dedicated trigger ('Invoices must be created with status draft') plus a full INSERT revoke; quotes, orders, and deliveries got neither. Consequences by table: deliveries — a sales_rep can INSERT a delivery born 'completed' (signature guard satisfied by any non-empty signed_by), producing a completed-delivery record that no RPC ever processed (no inventory movement, no order linkage effects; the delivery-items parent lock then prevents item rows, leaving an itemless completed delivery in driver boards/reports); quotes — a rep can INSERT a quote born 'accepted'/'declined'/'closed_short', skipping save_quote's 'New quotes must start with status draft' rule (that rule exists only inside the RPC); orders — admin-only INSERT, but an order born 'fulfilled'/'cancelled' skips the entire confirmation/inventory pipeline (this is the UPDATE-side sibling of the bulk-import lifecycle HIGH the Section 4 refresh fixed, which addressed only bulk_import_order's own status parameter).
confirmed.evidence: Invoices trigger: `IF NEW.status != 'draft' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invoices must be created with status draft. Got: %', NEW.status;` bound `BEFORE INSERT ON invoices`. No analogous `BEFORE INSERT` status trigger exists for quotes/orders/deliveries in any migration (transition triggers are declared `BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON <table>`). del_insert: `CREATE POLICY "del_insert" ON public.deliveries AS PERMISSIVE FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK ((is_admin() OR is_sales_rep()));` save_quote's draft rule is RPC-internal: `IF v_status <> 'draft' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'New quotes must start with status draft';`
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rep POSTs {order_id, customer_id, status:'completed', signed_by:'x', ...} to /rest/v1/deliveries. A completed delivery appears against a real order with zero delivered quantities and no inventory movement; cancel_order later refuses with ORDER_DELIVERY_QUANTITY_DRIFT ('completed delivery exists without delivered order-item quantity'), wedging the order's cancel path until an admin manually repairs the phantom row.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED. Every factual claim checks out against current migrations: (1) all four lifecycle transition triggers in 20260228300000_critical_prelaunch_fixes.sql are declared BEFORE UPDATE OF status only (orders ~390, deliveries ~413, invoices ~438, quotes ~463) and no later migration rebinds them to INSERT; (2) exhaustive search of every BEFORE INSERT trigger shows invoices alone got a born-draft trigger (20260302200000:30-48) plus a full authenticated write revoke (20260721014858:1778 — REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE ON invoices, invoice_items), while the only INSERT-arm triggers on deliveries are the signature guard (20260526151856:1531, satisfied by any non-empty signed_by) and period-open guards (20260716152906/172956/183442) whose INSERT branches allow a born-'completed' row in an open period; (3) the quotes draft rule is RPC-internal only (save_quote, latest 20260730235031:272) and the 20260730235031 revoke covers quote_sections/quote_items/customer_addresses, not quotes itself; (4) RLS permits the writes — del_insert = admin OR sales_rep (20260511060000:94-98), quotes_insert = admin or own rep (20260206174345:363-367); the finding is actually slightly understated: 20260210_fix_rls_critical_issues.sql:12-15 (sorts after 20260206174345) widened orders_insert to is_admin() OR is_sales_rep(), so orders are NOT admin-only — reps can insert born-'fulfilled' orders too; (5) the failure scenario is mechanically real — cancel_order in 20260721152604:109-121 raises ORDER_DELIVERY_QUANTITY_DRIFT exactly when a completed delivery exists without any order_items.quantity_delivered > 0, which a phantom born-completed delivery produces. Not in baseline: KNOWN_ISSUES.md's only insert-arm item is the profiles role lock (fixed 20260807215532), and the 2026-08-05 section-04 refresh addressed bulk_import_order's RPC status parameter, not direct PostgREST table INSERT. MED severity stands: exploitation needs an authenticated admin/rep credential making deliberate direct REST writes, and impact is lifecycle-integrity corruption plus a wedged cancel path rather than direct money movement — the same threat class the project closed for invoices as the 'Data API backdoor'.

confirmed.title: delivery_remainders has no transition enforcement — pending→fulfilled settable by direct update without a follow-up delivery
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260225200000_delivery_system_enhancements.sql:127-135 (del_rem_admin_all / del_rem_rep_update policies); .claude/schema-registry.json status_enums delivery_remainders.status; supabase/migrations/20260620130000_commission_batch_freeze_guard.sql:767-768 (the RPC-side transitions that can be bypassed)
confirmed.detail: delivery_remainders.status (pending/scheduled/fulfilled/cancelled) is the only Section-4 lifecycle status with no BEFORE UPDATE transition trigger at all (verified by trigger inventory; the 20260228300000 C3 set covers orders/deliveries/invoices/quotes/jobs/POs/returns but not delivery_remainders). RLS grants admins ALL and reps UPDATE. cancel_delivery/complete_delivery maintain remainders with careful rules (cancelled only when no followup_delivery_id, fulfilled when followup exists); a direct update can set any of the four statuses in any order — e.g. 'fulfilled' with followup_delivery_id NULL — silently dropping an owed remainder from the follow-up queue.
confirmed.evidence: Policies: `CREATE POLICY "del_rem_admin_all" ON delivery_remainders ... CREATE POLICY "del_rem_rep_update" ON delivery_remainders ...`; no `CREATE TRIGGER ... ON delivery_remainders` matching any enforce/transition pattern exists in migrations. RPC discipline it bypasses: `UPDATE delivery_remainders SET status = 'cancelled' ... WHERE ... AND followup_delivery_id IS NULL; UPDATE delivery_remainders SET status = 'fulfilled' ... AND followup_delivery_id IS NOT NULL;`
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rep marks a pending remainder 'fulfilled' directly (or a buggy client does). The customer's short-shipped quantity leaves the remainder queue with no follow-up delivery ever scheduled; the shortfall is never delivered or credited.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. No CREATE TRIGGER on delivery_remainders exists anywhere in supabase/migrations/ (multiline grep, zero matches); the C3 transition set in 20260228300000_critical_prelaunch_fixes.sql covers orders/deliveries/invoices/quotes/jobs/POs/returns only. Current RLS (del_rem_update in 20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:181-184, which superseded the finding's cited 20260225200000 policies — stale citation, same substance) grants UPDATE to any admin or sales_rep with no transition/column restriction, and the RPC-only table-write REVOKE in 20260716120104 covers only PO/AP tables, not delivery_remainders. The bypassed RPC discipline quoted from 20260620130000:767-768 matches source exactly. Not documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md or the 2026-08-05 section-04 gauntlet baseline (zero remainder mentions). Failure scenario requires a direct API write (no UI path mutates the table directly — frontend only reads and calls create_followup_delivery), which is consistent with the reviewer's LOW severity; severity stands.

confirmed.title: update_order_items status guard names nonexistent order status 'pending' (stale literal vs CHECK constraint)
confirmed.detail: The editability guard reads `IF v_order.status NOT IN ('confirmed', 'pending') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot edit order in status: %'`. Per .claude/schema-registry.json, orders.status CHECK allows only ['confirmed','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','voided'] — 'pending' cannot exist, so the branch is dead weight and the effective rule is confirmed-only. Behaviorally safe (fails closed), but it is a status literal that does not match the CHECK constraint (the class this audit was asked to flag). Caveat: the live invariant sweeps carry 3 allowlisted 'status-literals' rows (KNOWN_ISSUES §0f live-proof note); this may already be one of them — I could not verify the allowlist contents from the repo, so this may be known/accepted rather than new.
confirmed.evidence: `IF v_order.status NOT IN ('confirmed', 'pending') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot edit order in status: %', v_order.status; END IF;` vs schema-registry `orders.status => ['confirmed', 'partially_fulfilled', 'fulfilled', 'cancelled', 'voided']`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: No runtime failure (fails closed). Risk is maintenance: a future reader assumes a 'pending' order state exists, or a partially_fulfilled order edit is refused with a message implying 'pending' is reachable.

confirmed.title: Soft-deleting a planned quote orphans its active crop_program holds - no release on the delete exit path
confirmed.detail: The Quotes-list bulk delete only refuses quotes with order/job DRAWS; a planned quote in draft/sent/revised with active crop_program holds and zero draws passes the guard and is soft-deleted via a direct `.update({ deleted_at })`. Nothing releases its holds on this exit, and every downstream mechanism is blind to it: (1) the hold-release trigger is `AFTER UPDATE OF status` so a deleted_at-only UPDATE never fires it; (2) `_sync_planned_holds` early-returns 0 on a deleted quote (its release branch is only reachable for live quotes); (3) `release_expired_quote_holds` (called from src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:329) releases only holds whose quote status is declined/expired - a deleted quote keeps its non-terminal status; (4) `auto_expire_quotes` filters `deleted_at IS NULL` and `is_planned = false` (20260614143649:36,49); (5) the integrity sentinel's `stale_quote_hold` alert requires a TERMINAL quote status, so a deleted draft/sent/revised quote is invisible to it. Checked the migrations directly: there is NO trigger on quotes covering deleted_at and no `_guard_quote_delete` (the guard roster has `_guard_order_delete`, `_guard_invoice_delete`, `_guard_delivery_delete`, `_guard_po_delete` - no quote variant), so the DB neither releases the holds nor blocks the delete. Impact of the orphan: it is counted by `holds_qty` in get_inventory_position (20260716120120:53-62, shown as Held / Total Planned on InventoryPage and as On Hold in ReceivingHubPanel.tsx:296), it reduces the dispatch stock-status 'free' computation which subtracts ALL active non-expired holds (20260702178000_layer2_dispatch_free_precision.sql:70-98), it tightens the manual-hold free-stock warning (InventoryPage.tsx:393-396), and it feeds the inventory forecast. If the hold's section had no needed_by_date, expires_at is NULL and the phantom reservation NEVER date-expires. Only remedy is an admin manually clicking Release on the InventoryPage holds tab (`release_inventory_hold` permits crop_program holds, 20260702182000:53-56), but nothing labels the hold as belonging to a deleted quote. Note the no-auto-expire policy for planned quotes (owner gate G-AE) actively pushes staff toward deletion as the cleanup gesture, making this path likely in practice. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md or the 2026-08-05 Section 4 refresh (PARKED-03 was the distinct quick-delivery prebook leak, resolved).

confirmed.title: Planned holds with no needed_by_date get NULL expires_at: invisible to the forecast and expiring-holds alerts, and never expire

This is the same class that makes finding 1's orphans permanent, but it also affects LIVE open planned quotes: a dateless planned program is a reservation that shrinks displayed free stock while being invisible to the very forecasting screens meant to explain where the demand comes from. The DB does not enforce needed_by_date for planned quotes (checked: no CHECK/trigger on quote_sections and no validation in save_quote or _sync_planned_holds).

confirmed.title: rollover_quote_to_season creates the new planned booking with zero holds and drops needed_by_date; old booking's holds stay active, double-counting demand

Until the old booking is manually closed (close short / cancel), the same remainder demand is counted twice across the two seasons' quotes in planned/held displays. confirmed.title: Crop-program holds are unchecked soft holds: creation never checks stock, nothing blocks overselling, and excess surfaces only on the Forecast tab
confirmed.detail: Checked the migrations: _sync_planned_holds and create_planned_holds perform no inventory read whatsoever, and net_position is `quantity_available - quantity_prebooked + quantity_on_order` - active holds are deliberately NOT subtracted (documented in src/types/index.ts:1007). The only stock-vs-hold warning in the product is for MANUAL holds on InventoryPage (todaysFree check); marking a quote planned in QuoteBuilder produces no shortage indication at all (searched QuoteBuilder - no shortfall/exceed check on the planned path), and the Forecast tab is the sole surface comparing planned demand to available+on_order - which misses undated holds entirely (finding 3). This soft-hold model is plausibly intended (the Layer 2 owner decision for job holds was explicitly 'WARN, never block', and holds are described as forecast bookkeeping), but the WARN half is not implemented for crop programs: there is no warn at mark-planned time and no over-held indicator on InventoryPage. Reporting so the intended/unintended call can be made explicitly.

confirmed.title: Quotes-list delete guard misses planned quotes with active zero-draw scheduled jobs
confirmed.detail: The delete guard checks quote_product_draws and job_product_draws for quantity_drawn > 0. A scheduled/in_progress job attached to the quote whose demand drew nothing from the booking (its chemicals are not among the quote's items, so the crop pool for those products is 0 and _sync_quote_job_reservations writes a 'job' hold but no draw row) leaves no draw evidence, so the quote soft-deletes while the job remains scheduled and dispatched, referencing a hidden quote. The job's own 'job' hold survives correctly (source_id = job_id, released by the job lifecycle), but the operational link is broken: QuoteBuilder can no longer be opened to see or manage the booking the job descends from, and the close_quote_as_short active-jobs refusal (20260706030000:92-98) that protects the status-based exits has no counterpart on the delete exit. Narrow edge (requires a job whose products diverge from the quote's items), reported for completeness of the exit-path matrix.
confirmed.evidence: Quotes.tsx:388-389: `supabase.from('quote_product_draws').select('quote_id').in('quote_id', ids).gt('quantity_drawn', 0), supabaseUntyped.from('job_product_draws').select('quote_id').in('quote_id', ids).gt('quantity_drawn', 0)` - existence of scheduled jobs themselves is never checked, unlike the closed_short trigger guard: `IF NEW.status = 'closed_short' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jobs WHERE quote_id = NEW.id AND deleted_at IS NULL AND status IN ('scheduled','in_progress'))`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A planned booking has one scheduled job whose recipe products differ from the quote lines (zero draws). Staff delete the quote; the job stays on the dispatch board holding stock for a booking nobody can open, and cancelling/completing the job later resyncs against a deleted quote (safe but confusing: crop pool 0, draws dropped).

verdict.reason: Confirmed against current source. (1) The delete guard at src/pages/Quotes.tsx:387-400 checks only quote_product_draws and job_product_draws with .gt('quantity_drawn', 0); it never checks for scheduled/in_progress jobs themselves — quoted code matches the finding verbatim. (2) The zero-draw mechanism is real: in _sync_quote_job_reservations (20260706030000:246-296, preserved in the latest version 20260710120000:239-244), a job product absent from quote_items yields v_booking=0 → v_crop_pool=0 → v_draw=LEAST(demand,0)=0, and the job_product_draws INSERT is gated by `IF v_draw > 0`, while the 'job' inventory_hold is written unconditionally for v_hold=demand>0 — so an active job can exist with zero draw evidence. (3) The asymmetry with the status exits is real: both close_quote_as_short (20260706030000:377-383) and the direct-status trigger guard (:92-98, `IF NEW.status = 'closed_short' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jobs WHERE quote_id = NEW.id AND deleted_at IS NULL AND status IN ('scheduled','in_progress'))`) refuse active jobs; the soft-delete exit (plain UPDATE of deleted_at) has no counterpart. (4) I checked the migrations for a DB-side enforcement the reviewer might have missed: every trigger on quotes fires on UPDATE OF status or commission_split (plus a row_version bump that checks nothing); _enforce_quote_status_transition early-returns when status is unchanged; no later migration adds a deleted_at guard — so the DB does not enforce this (checked, not merely unfound). (5) Post-delete behavior matches: _sync_quote_job_reservations looks up the quote with `deleted_at IS NULL`, so a later job cancel/complete resyncs gracefully with crop_pool=0 — "safe but confusing" as stated. (6) Not in the baseline: KNOWN_ISSUES.md has no match for the quote delete guard / zero-draw job gap, and the 2026-08-05 section-04 doc's only Quotes.tsx mention is the convert_quote_to_order caller; no mention of active jobs or the delete exit. Severity LOW is correct: the edge requires every active job on the quote to have drawn nothing (any single positive draw row blocks the delete), inventory stays correct (the 'job' hold is keyed to the job and released by the job lifecycle), and the impact is an orphaned operational link (job on the dispatch board referencing a hidden quote), not money or stock corruption.

confirmed.title: Caller-controlled cost/profit still drives commission basis on convert_quote_to_order and create_direct_order — the exact class hardened out of bulk_import_order remains open on the two main order-creation seams
confirmed.detail: The 2026-08-05/06 bulk-import hardening (six live migrations, per the Section 4 gauntlet doc) established that 'a sales rep could submit an explicit low cost to inflate the newly created commission liability' is a real, Sol-confirmed blocker, and fixed it by making products.current_cost the authoritative cost and commission basis — for bulk_import_order ONLY. The same attack remains fully open on the two canonical order-creation seams: (1) save_quote inserts client-supplied `current_cost`, `profit`, and `total_price` verbatim into quote_items with no recomputation, no reconciliation against products.current_cost, and no check that profit = (price − cost) × qty; its server totals are just SUM of those client values; convert_quote_to_order then calls `_insert_commissions_for_order(v_order_id, v_quote.customer_id, v_quote.total_profit, ...)` — commission basis is entirely client-controlled. (2) create_direct_order computes v_total_cost/v_total_profit from caller-supplied `unit_cost` in the items JSON and passes that profit straight to `_insert_commissions_for_order`; NewOrder.tsx even exposes unit_cost as an editable input (line 895-898), so this needs no API access at all. There are no quote_items triggers (grep for CREATE TRIGGER on quote_items returns nothing), and the order_items cost snapshot trigger only records `cost_at_time_cents` passively — its own COMMENT says cost_per_unit 'is caller-supplied and may be a stale quote cost or manual override' and nothing reads the snapshot for commission math at creation time. Checked the migrations: the DB does not enforce Product-authoritative cost on these paths (this is a verified absence, not a failure to find). Not listed in docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md; the Section 4 doc explicitly scoped the fix to bulk_import_order and called the normal paths 'otherwise aligned'.
confirmed.evidence: save_quote (20260730235031): `COALESCE((v_item->>'current_cost')::numeric, 0), ... COALESCE((v_item->>'profit')::numeric, 0), COALESCE((v_item->>'total_price')::numeric, 0)` inserted verbatim; convert (20260702172500:207-210): `PERFORM _insert_commissions_for_order(v_order_id, v_quote.customer_id, v_quote.total_profit, v_quote.commission_split, current_date);`; create_direct_order (20260614142939:122-124): `v_total_cost := v_total_cost + COALESCE((v_item->>'quantity')::numeric, 0) * COALESCE((v_item->>'unit_cost')::numeric, 0);` then `:190-193 PERFORM _insert_commissions_for_order(v_order_id, p_customer_id, v_total_profit, ...)`; contrast 20260806000752_authorize_bulk_import_product_cost.sql ('validates supplied legacy cost but always uses Product current_cost').
confirmed.failure_scenario: An active sales_rep calls save_quote (or uses NewOrder's unit-cost field / calls create_direct_order via PostgREST with their own JWT) with cost 0 or profit inflated on each line, converts the quote, and the system creates commission rows from the inflated profit — overstating commission liability, margin reporting, and financial_audit_log total_impact_cents. verdict.reason: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — the create_direct_order half is real; the save_quote half is refuted. Refuted: save_quote (latest def 20260730235031) does NOT keep client cost/profit — immediately after the quoted insert loop (lines ~317-346), a server-authoritative CTE (lines ~350-428) recomputes every line from products.current_cost ('COALESCE(p.current_cost, 0) AS cc', 'ROUND((ppu - cc) * total_units, 2) AS profit') and overwrites quote_items (UPDATE ... SET current_cost = f.cc, profit = f.profit), then quotes.total_profit is summed from those recomputed rows (lines ~467-503). So the commission basis convert_quote_to_order passes (v_quote.total_profit) is server-computed; the 'cost 0 via save_quote → convert' attack cannot occur. The only client lever is price_override — a deliberate feature (20260528042000) that also raises the customer's billed price. Confirmed: create_direct_order's latest definition (20260614142939, no later supersession — 20260805211951 mentions it only in a comment) computes v_total_cost from caller-supplied unit_cost (lines ~118-126) and passes v_total_profit to _insert_commissions_for_order (~:193), whose latest version (20260722174029:404+) uses p_order_profit verbatim; the role gate (20260610142204:54) admits sales_rep; NewOrder.tsx:516 calls the RPC with item.unit_cost from an editable input (:891-901); no quote_items/order-cost reconciliation trigger exists (verified absence — grep of all migrations); not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md, and the section-04 doc (lines 11, 38) scoped the Product-cost-authoritative fix to bulk import while calling this migration canonical. confirmed.title: Quick-delivery invoice posted before completion is never adjusted on partial completion, and the follow-up delivery auto-invoice then bills the shortfall a second time; the 2026-03 admin 'posted invoice may need adjustment' notification was silently dropped
confirmed.detail: create_quick_delivery creates a draft invoice for the FULL requested quantities at delivery-creation time (delivery still 'scheduled'). post_invoice has no guard tying posting to delivery completion — I inspected the current wrapper chain (20260721145936 → 20260716224000 → 20260714224000) and found role/status/pricing guards but no delivered-vs-billed reconciliation and no delivery-status check (verified absence in those three layers; earlier impl layers not exhaustively read). complete_delivery's partial-completion invoice adjustment loop filters `status = 'draft'` only, so a posted invoice keeps billing the full quantity after a partial completion. The pre-U2 complete_delivery (20260302200000) explicitly notified admins in this exact case ('posted invoice … may need adjustment'); the current body contains zero occurrences of that notification — the safety net regressed silently. Worse, when the remainder is later delivered via a follow-up delivery, the auto-invoice guard `(delivery_id = p_delivery_id OR delivery_id IS NULL)` does not match the original delivery's invoice, so a NEW invoice is auto-created for the remainder quantity — which the already-posted invoice also bills.

confirmed.title: convert_quote_to_order copies live quote rows, never the sent/accepted quote_versions snapshot — a quote edited after send ('revised', or a DB-level sent→sent item rewrite) converts at prices the customer never saw
confirmed.detail: convert_quote_to_order builds order_items directly `FROM quote_items` and copies quote-header totals; it never reads quote_versions and never verifies that live rows still match the last sent snapshot. Two paths make live rows diverge from what the customer accepted: (1) Sanctioned path — status 'revised' is editable in the UI (canEdit includes 'revised') AND convertible (canConvert and the RPC's `status NOT IN ('sent','revised','accepted')` gate both allow 'revised'), and the workflow doc says a new snapshot is only created 'on next send' — so a revised-but-never-resent quote converts at edited prices with no snapshot of what was converted. (2) DB-level path — save_quote's transition matrix only runs `IF v_status IS DISTINCT FROM v_old_status`, so a sent→sent save (same status) skips validation entirely and rewrites every section/item at new prices while `sent_at` is preserved; no guard I could find prevents item rewrites while status stays 'sent' (the UI blocks it — canEdit excludes 'sent' — but the SECURITY DEFINER RPC does not; a quote owner via PostgREST can do it). The doc's own 'common mistakes' list warns 'Changing product prices after a quote was sent (the snapshot preserves the original)' — but the snapshot only preserves evidence; conversion, ordering, delivery, and invoicing all flow from the mutable rows.
confirmed.evidence: convert (20260702172500:126-179): `INSERT INTO order_items ... SELECT ... qi.price_per_unit, qi.current_cost, ... FROM quote_items qi JOIN quote_sections qs ... WHERE qi.quote_id = p_quote_id` — no quote_versions reference anywhere in the body; :120 `IF v_quote.status NOT IN ('sent', 'revised', 'accepted') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'BOOKING_CLOSED...'`; save_quote (20260730235031:242): `IF v_status IS DISTINCT FROM v_old_status THEN` guards the only transition check; QuoteBuilder.tsx:445 `const canEdit = ['draft', 'revised'].includes(currentStatus);` :455 `const canConvert = ['sent', 'revised', 'accepted'].includes(currentStatus);`
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rep sends a quote at $10/unit (v1 snapshot), customer verbally accepts. Rep flips to 'revised', raises to $11/unit, and clicks Convert without re-sending. The order, delivery, and invoice all carry $11; no quote_versions snapshot contains $11, so the dispute trail shows the customer accepted $10. Same result via a direct sent→sent save_quote API call with rewritten items, with the quote still displaying as an untouched 'sent' quote.

verdict.reason: Factually confirmed against current source: convert_quote_to_order (latest definition = 20260702172500, no later migration redefines it) builds order_items FROM live quote_items (:167-179) with no quote_versions reference, and allows 'revised' (:120); QuoteBuilder.tsx:445/:455 canEdit includes 'revised' and canConvert includes 'revised'; save_quote (latest = 20260730235031) runs its transition matrix only IF v_status IS DISTINCT FROM v_old_status (:241), so a sent→sent save rewrites all items with no DB guard (only status-transition triggers exist on quotes; KNOWN_ISSUES ~line 217 shows draft→sent→sent is a deliberately supported save path); create_quote_version fires only on send/email, never in the convert handlers (QuoteBuilder.tsx:2434-2513). Not documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor in the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline (whose sole finding is the Bulk Order Import bypass). However, severity is corrected to LOW: (1) the 'sanctioned path' half is documented intended design — QUOTE_TO_DELIVERY.md:34-35 explicitly defines 'revised' as edits-after-send with snapshot deferred to next send, and converting a revised quote at revised prices is the normal verbal-renegotiation flow; the system nowhere promises conversion matches the last-sent snapshot; (2) the evidence-loss claim is overstated — order_items durably snapshots conversion-time prices with quote_item_id linkage, and financial_audit_log records converted totals (20260702172500:212-230), so the trail does show sent-v1 $10 / revised / order $11; (3) the DB-level sent→sent rewrite is owner-or-admin-only (NOT_QUOTE_OWNER + active-role gates), requires the current row_version, bumps row_version/updated_at, and its only marginal harm over the sanctioned revised path is concealing the 'revised' status label — an insider-concealment hardening gap, not a money-math or privilege defect.

confirmed.title: save_quote and create_direct_order accept NaN/Infinity in money and quantity fields — bulk import rejects them, these seams poison orders that later fail at invoice time
confirmed.detail: The 2026-08-05 Sol review established that PostgreSQL numeric accepts 'NaN'/'Infinity'/'-Infinity' and blocked the bulk-import migration until they were explicitly rejected. Neither save_quote nor create_direct_order gained that guard: both cast payload strings straight to numeric (grep for NaN/Infinity/is_finite in 20260730235031 returns 0 matches; create_direct_order likewise has none). A NaN price/quantity/profit flows into quote_items → quote totals → (via convert) orders/order_items — orders.total_price/total_profit are plain numerics that store NaN. convert_quote_to_order would fail late at `ROUND(v_quote.total_price * 100)::bigint` (NaN cannot cast to bigint), aborting conversion with an opaque error; create_direct_order has no cents cast at all, so a NaN order commits successfully and every later invoice creation (`round(v_item.total_price * 100)::bigint`) fails, leaving an order that can never be billed, with NaN commissions attempted.
confirmed.evidence: save_quote: `(v_item->>'actual_rate')::numeric`, `COALESCE((v_item->>'profit')::numeric, 0)` etc. with no finiteness checks; create_direct_order: `COALESCE((v_item->>'quantity')::numeric, 0) * COALESCE((v_item->>'price_per_unit')::numeric, 0)`; contrast the applied bulk-import follow-up 20260805220757 which 'rejects all non-finite quantity/price/cost values and rounds unit and extended dollar amounts to cents before writes' (Section 4 doc line 56).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A buggy or malicious client sends `{"quantity": "NaN"}` to create_direct_order. The order, order_items, inventory prebook of NaN units, and inventory_transactions rows all commit (NaN propagates through numeric arithmetic); inventory.quantity_prebooked for that product becomes NaN, corrupting Net Position for every later quote/order of that product, and any attempt to invoice the order errors with 'cannot convert NaN to bigint'.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED against current source. (1) Latest save_quote is 20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql (no later migration redefines it); its item loop (lines ~317-346) casts payload text straight to numeric — `COALESCE((v_item->>'price_per_unit')::numeric, 0)`, `(v_item->>'actual_rate')::numeric`, `(v_item->>'acres')::numeric`, `COALESCE((v_item->>'profit')::numeric, 0)` — with zero finiteness checks (grep for NaN/Infinity/is_finite in the file matches only 'finance'/'maintenance' substrings). (2) Latest create_direct_order is 20260614142939 (no later redefinition); it computes `v_qty := COALESCE((v_item->>'quantity')::numeric, 0)` and guards only `IF v_qty <= 0 THEN CONTINUE` — in PostgreSQL numeric, NaN compares GREATER than all non-NaN values, so 'NaN'::numeric passes both this guard and the table constraint `chk_inventory_qty_prebooked CHECK (quantity_prebooked >= 0)` (20260209200000:20); it then executes `quantity_prebooked = quantity_prebooked + (v_item->>'quantity')::numeric`, which yields NaN and corrupts Net Position. No trigger on quote_items/order_items/inventory validates finiteness (only total-recompute and cost-snapshot triggers exist). (3) The only non-finite guard in the entire migration set is 20260805220757 (`v_qty::text IN ('NaN','Infinity','-Infinity')`, lines 116-120), which covers bulk import only. (4) Downstream failure points verified: latest convert_quote_to_order (20260702172500:224) has `ROUND(v_quote.total_price * 100)::bigint` (NaN→bigint raises), and invoice creation (20260614150249:106,113) has `round(v_item.total_price * 100)::bigint`, so a NaN direct order commits but can never be invoiced. (5) Not in the baseline: KNOWN_ISSUES.md and the 2026-08-05 section-04 doc discuss non-finite rejection exclusively for the bulk-import RPC; neither mentions the save_quote/create_direct_order gap. The failure scenario is real for any authenticated admin/sales_rep client sending the JSON string "NaN" ('NaN'::numeric is a valid cast). MED severity is appropriate: requires a buggy/malicious authenticated client, impact is inventory/AR integrity corruption requiring manual cleanup, not direct money loss.

confirmed.title: Cent-rounding formula differs across the three invoice-line paths for the same delivered quantity
confirmed.detail: Line totals for identical economic facts are computed three ways: quick delivery uses `safe_cents_qty(unit_cents, qty)`; the delivery auto-invoice uses `ROUND(quantity_delivered * price_per_unit * 100)` (dollars first, one round); the partial-completion adjustment rewrites the same line as `ROUND(di.quantity_delivered * ii.unit_price_cents)` (cents-basis). For fractional quantities with sub-cent unit prices these differ by a cent (e.g. price 10.005, qty 3: round(3×10.005×100)=3002 vs 3×round(10.005×100)=3003). Header cost totals similarly differ: creators use ROUND(cost×qty×100) while the partial recompute uses SUM(cost_cents × quantity). Self-consistent per invoice (header is recomputed from lines where it matters) but a partial completion can shift an already-created line by a cent versus what a full completion would have billed, and cross-path cent drift shows up in reconciliation against orders.total_price.
confirmed.evidence: :273 `extended_cents = ROUND(di.quantity_delivered * ii.unit_price_cents)` vs :417 `ROUND(v_item.quantity_delivered * v_item.price_per_unit * 100)::bigint` vs quick delivery `safe_cents_qty(v_item_price_cents, v_item_qty)`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Delivery of 3 units at $10.005 invoiced via auto-invoice bills 3002 cents; the same 3 units on a partially-completed quick delivery are re-extended to 3003 cents; AR reconciliation against the order total shows a 1-cent unexplained variance per affected line.

verdict.reason: All three cited formulas verified verbatim in current source: 20260716120104:273 (ROUND(qty * unit_price_cents), cents-basis partial rewrite), :417 (ROUND(qty * price_per_unit * 100), dollars-first auto-invoice), and 20260706130000:225 (safe_cents_qty(price_cents, qty), quick delivery). Later migrations (20260716173342/191000/202000 for complete_delivery; 20260803010917 for create_quick_delivery) only rename-and-wrap the implementations for authorization/preflight/idempotency — the arithmetic is unchanged and live. The failure scenario is real: order_items.price_per_unit is unconstrained numeric with no rounding trigger, so sub-cent unit prices can reach these paths, and for such prices dollars-first vs cents-basis rounding differ by a cent (3×$10.005 → 3002 vs 3003 cents, valid under Postgres half-away-from-zero rounding). Not previously documented: KNOWN_ISSUES.md covers a different rounding issue (parked split-billing Feature B independent-rounding blocker) and the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline covers bulk_import_order sub-cent normalization only. Severity LOW is correct — divergence requires sub-cent prices or the fractional-qty partial path, is cent-scale, and each invoice remains internally self-consistent.

confirmed.title: create_direct_order skips the customer-active check that quick delivery enforces
confirmed.detail: create_quick_delivery raises 'Customer is inactive' (`IF NOT v_customer.is_active`); create_direct_order only checks existence, so a confirmed order with inventory prebooking and commissions can be created for a deactivated customer. confirmed.title: create_direct_order performs no cent rounding anywhere — fractional-cent money stored in order_items/orders and commissions minted from the unrounded profit accumulator
confirmed.detail: The latest on-disk create_direct_order (the path NewOrder.tsx uses for priced orders) accumulates header totals and inserts order_items.total_price / profit / net_margin as raw numeric qty*price with no ROUND(...,2) at any point. The header is later rewritten by trg_recalc_order_totals with ROUND(SUM(lines),2), so orders.total_price = round-of-sum while invoicing bills sum-of-round (extended_cents = round(line*100) per line, 20260620190000:104,111 and 20260721014858:488), letting order header vs sum-of-invoice-line-cents drift by cents on multi-line fractional orders. Commissions are minted at line 190-193 from the UNROUNDED v_total_profit accumulator, not the trigger-canonical rounded stored profit — the exact class the Section-4 gauntlet forced bulk_import_order to fix ('whole-cent per line', 'commissions from trigger-canonical stored profit', migrations 20260806004644/20260806012423); the canonical direct-order path itself was never given the same treatment. Quote-converted orders don't have this problem (save_quote rounds each line to 2dp server-side).
confirmed.evidence: 20260614142939:119-121: `v_total_price := v_total_price + COALESCE((v_item->>'quantity')::numeric, 0) * COALESCE((v_item->>'price_per_unit')::numeric, 0);` (no ROUND); :162: total_price inserted as `COALESCE((v_item->>'quantity')::numeric, 0) * COALESCE((v_item->>'price_per_unit')::numeric, 0)`; :190-193: `PERFORM _insert_commissions_for_order(v_order_id, p_customer_id, v_total_profit, v_customer.default_commission_split, p_order_date);` — v_total_profit is the unrounded accumulator. confirmed.failure_scenario: Direct order: 3 lines of qty 3.33 at $10.10 → each line total_price stored 33.633 (sub-cent). orders.total_price = ROUND(100.899,2) = 100.90; invoice for full delivery bills 3 × round(3363.3) = 10090 — here equal, but with half-cent lines (e.g. qty 2.5 × $10.01 = 25.025 per line, 3 lines: header ROUND(75.075)=75.08 vs invoice 3×round(2502.5)=3×2503=7509 = 75.09) the order total and the invoiced total disagree by a cent, and commission basis differs sub-cent from stored order profit.
