confirmed.title: CommissionPayments payout picker and payment list are hard-capped (500/200 rows) with no pagination or truncation warning
confirmed.detail: fetchUnpaid loads pending commissions ordered by order_date desc with `.limit(500)`, and fetchPayments loads `.limit(200)` payments, with no count check, pagination, or truncation indicator. Once more than 500 pending commissions exist, the OLDEST pending commissions (beyond the newest 500 by order_date) silently disappear from the payout picker — precisely the rows most at risk of being forgotten — and the per-recipient '(N unpaid)' counts and selected totals understate. Same for payments beyond 200: the Unposted/Posted summary card totals (computed client-side from the fetched page, lines 425-430) silently under-report.
confirmed.evidence: CommissionPayments.tsx:163-165: `.eq('status', 'pending').order('order_date', { ascending: false }).limit(500);` and :90-91: `.order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(200);` — no `count:'exact'` or overflow handling on either.
confirmed.failure_scenario: After two busy seasons, 620 commissions are pending. The 120 oldest (last year's) never appear in the New Payment modal for any recipient; nobody is told they were truncated; those reps' old commissions sit unpaid indefinitely while the screen looks complete.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED — every element of the claim checks out against current source, and I could not find any mechanism elsewhere that mitigates it.

Code verification (src/pages/CommissionPayments.tsx, 839 lines total):
- :83-91 `fetchPayments`: `supabase.from('commission_payments').select('*').order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(200);` — no `count:'exact'`, no range/pagination, no overflow branch. Quoted exactly as the reviewer states.
- :154-165 `fetchUnpaid`: `.from('commissions').select(...).eq('status','pending').order('order_date', { ascending: false }).limit(500);` — same, no count or overflow handling. Sort is DESC on `order_date`, so the rows dropped are indeed the OLDEST pending commissions, exactly as claimed.
- Downstream dependence on the truncated arrays is real and client-side only: :249-252 `recipients` is built from `unpaidCommissions`; :254-256 `recipientCommissions = unpaidCommissions.filter(c => c.recipient_user_id === selectedRecipient)` (client-side filter over the global top-500 — there is no per-recipient server query, so one recipient's list is capped by other recipients' newer rows); :258-260 `selectedTotal` reduces over that filtered set; :726-728 renders `{r.name} ({unpaidCommissions.filter(...).length} unpaid)`; :739 `Unpaid Commissions ({recipientCommissions.length})`; :774 "No unpaid commissions for this recipient" is shown whenever the recipient has zero rows in the fetched page, which is indistinguishable from truncation.
- :424-430 confirms the payments-side claim: `const unpostedTotal = payments.filter(p => p.status === 'unposted').reduce(...)` and the same for `postedTotal` — both computed over the 200-row page, so the summary cards under-report once payments exceed 200. Note the tab filter at :423 (`payments.filter(p => p.status === tab)`) means the Voided tab is also fed from the same shared 200-row page ordered by `created_at`, so a heavily-voided history can starve the Unposted tab of rows — a slight aggravation the reviewer did not mention.

No missed enforcement mechanism:
- No other read path substitutes. `grep "from('commissions')"` across src returns only four callers: CommissionPayments.tsx:155, Reports.tsx:214, notificationTriggers.ts:576, reconciliation.ts:780. Reports.tsx:213-218 is a date-ranged report view (`select('*').order('order_date',...)`, no explicit limit) and does not create payouts. Payment creation is only reachable from the modal's `selectedCommissions` set, which is sourced entirely from the capped `fetchUnpaid` result — so a truncated commission is genuinely unpayable through the UI until the newer rows ahead of it are paid off.
- No server-side guard exists or could exist: this is a pure client query shape, so no migration, trigger, or RPC can compensate. I checked the commission-creation path (`_insert_commissions_for_order`, supabase/migrations/20260722174029_commission_split_recipient_ids.sql:404-506) only to confirm `order_date` is always populated on both the order and job channels (`p_order_date date DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE`, written at :475 and :504) — so the DESC sort is well-defined and NULL-ordering does not accidentally rescue old rows.

Not already documented. `docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` contains no entry about UI row caps, `.limit()`, pagination, or truncation on any list screen (the only "cap" entry is the unrelated Phase 3C git-ancestry `MAX_HISTORY_COMMITS` item at :1029). The 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline contains no `limit`/pagination/truncation material at all. Every prior CommissionPayments finding across docs/ is a different defect: the cancelled-commission leak (LEDGER.json:347 `lifecycle:CommissionPayments.fetchUnpaid:cancelled-leak`, the `.eq('status','pending')` fix that is now the line immediately above the cap), the blank order#/customer display fix (LEDGER.json:842, "RESOLVED" in the 2026-08-05 §4 doc line 934), the NULL-recipient "Other" HIGH (gauntlet 2026-07-22 sections-05-08:45), and the void dead-order count (codex-driven LEDGER.json:89). None touches row caps.

Severity: LOW is correct and should not be raised. The failure requires >500 simultaneously-pending commissions; the overnight-bug-hunt live evidence in docs/audits/overnight-bug-hunt/LEDGER.json:639 records "32 pending, 0 paid" on live, so this is latent and volume-gated, not currently firing. It is nonetheless a real silent-money-loss shape rather than a cosmetic nit — the rows that vanish are the oldest unpaid liabilities, the screen gives no indication of truncation, and the fix is small (`count:'exact'` plus a banner or range pagination, and a per-recipient server-side filter for the picker).

confirmed.title: Void-payment modal copy omits the job-channel close-out rule — admin is told dead-ORDER rows close out, not dead-minting-INVOICE rows
confirmed.detail: The void confirmation modal says linked commissions 'will be reset to pending ... except any whose order was since cancelled or voided, which will be closed out'. Since U8, void_commission_payment ALSO permanently closes out (cancelled, amount 0) any job-sourced commission whose minting invoice is no longer live — a condition the modal never mentions. An admin voiding a batch containing job commissions whose invoice was cancelled expects them back as pending per the modal, but they are closed out. The post-void toast does report the aggregate counts, but attributes them only to 'order cancelled/voided' (line 401), which is wrong for job rows.
confirmed.evidence: CommissionPayments.tsx:668-669: 'except any whose order was since cancelled or voided, which will be closed out (not re-payable)' — DB (20260707060000:1670-1680): cancel branch also fires on `c.job_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i WHERE i.id = c.invoice_id AND i.status NOT IN ('voided','cancelled') AND i.deleted_at IS NULL)`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A batch holds job J-88's pending commissions; J-88's invoice was cancelled (rows already cancelled) or the batch's job rows reference a since-voided invoice. Admin reads the modal, expects reset-to-pending, voids, and gets 'closed out (order cancelled/voided)' messaging for rows whose ORDER concept doesn't even apply — misdiagnosing what happened and possibly re-invoicing the job expecting old rows to revive.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED — the claim survives every refutation angle I tried. 1) Source text is quoted accurately. src/pages/CommissionPayments.tsx:668-669: "Its {voidTarget?.item_count ?? 'unverified number of'} linked commission(s) will be reset to pending and can be re-paid later — / except any whose order was since cancelled or voided, which will be closed out (not re-payable)." The toast at :401 is likewise `${resetCount} commission(s) reset to pending, ${cancelledCount} closed out (order cancelled/voided)` — the ONLY reason surfaced is order deadness. 2) DB behavior is as claimed, and I verified it in the CURRENT definition, not a superseded one. supabase/migrations/20260707060000_u8_application_channel_commissions.sql:1655-1681 — the cancel branch fires on `EXISTS (orders o ... cancelled/voided/deleted_at)` OR `(c.job_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i WHERE i.id = c.invoice_id AND i.status NOT IN ('voided','cancelled') AND i.deleted_at IS NULL))`, and the reset branch excludes the same job-lineage condition plus `AND c.status <> 'cancelled'`. So a job row is closed out (status 'cancelled', commission_amount 0) for a reason the modal never names. 3) Supersession check (migrations apply in timestamp order): `grep -rln void_commission_payment supabase/migrations/` returns 14 files; the only two later than 20260707060000 (20260720233000_per_line_split_billing_save_rpc.sql:1556 and 20260721180000_fix_split_impl_unassigned_app_service_record.sql:1239) mention it only inside a comment about `commission_payment_items.commission_id` FK behavior — neither redefines the function. The earlier 20260622070000_void_commission_payment_dead_order_guard.sql is the order-only ancestor that the U8 file replaced. 20260707060000 is the live body. 4) The scenario can occur. Job-sourced commissions really do enter these batches: fetchUnpaid selects `job_id` (CommissionPayments.tsx:157) and labels rows `Job ${...}` (:227-228), so a batch can contain rows with NO order at all — for which the modal's "whose order was since cancelled or voided" is not merely incomplete but categorically inapplicable. The dead-invoice condition is reachable post-batch (invoice voided/cancelled after the batch was created or posted); a row already flipped to 'cancelled' while sitting in the batch is likewise excluded from reset and counted in v_cancelled_count. 5) Not already documented. docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md mentions void_commission_payment only at line 937 (the 2026-06-22 order-deadness guard, marked fixed) — nothing about the U8 job/invoice branch or the modal copy. docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md (101 lines) is entirely about bulk_import_order and never touches commission-payment voiding. Severity: LOW is correct and I would not raise it. The DB does the right thing deliberately (the Codex R1 P1 comment at :1644-1647 shows generation-precise `c.invoice_id` testing is intentional — re-invoicing mints a NEW commission generation), so there is no money or data error. The harm is confined to operator misdiagnosis, and the finding's tail speculation ("possibly re-invoicing the job expecting old rows to revive") overstates it, since re-invoicing produces correct fresh commissions regardless. Real, but purely a user-facing copy/messaging accuracy defect in both the modal (:668-669) and the toast reason string (:401).

confirmed.title: update_order_items idempotent replay is not payload-bound — edited items silently reported as saved on retry after a lost response
confirmed.detail: The public update_order_items wrapper replays a cached receipt keyed only by (key, operation) — no request fingerprint, no actor binding, unlike save_invoice/create_quick_delivery which were hardened by 20260803010917 exactly against this class ('avoids… silently treating edited input as saved'). Checked all migrations: no later migration adds binding for update_order_items (grep for ARGUMENT_MISMATCH/request_fingerprint finds none naming it). Frontend keeps the same key on failure (useIdempotencyKey resets only on confirmed success, OrderDetail.tsx:523), which is correct for retries of the SAME payload but combines with the unbound replay to drop CHANGED payloads.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Office user saves order-item edits; the RPC commits but the response is lost (network drop), so resetKey() never runs. User re-opens the editor, changes a quantity or price, clicks Save again. The same key is sent; the wrapper returns the first save's cached result before any mutation (20260714221000:39), assertRpcResult passes, and the UI toasts 'Order updated' — the second edit (money- and inventory-affecting: update_order_items adjusts prebooked inventory and totals) is silently discarded while being reported as saved.

verdict.reason:
NOT REFUTED as a mechanism, but the stated failure scenario is factually wrong in its main step and the impact is narrower than claimed, so severity drops HIGH → MED.

What holds up (verified myself):
1. Current definition of public.update_order_items is the wrapper in supabase/migrations/20260714221000_order_and_cycle_count_concurrency_guards.sql:11-89. Its replay is key+operation only: ":37-40 `IF p_idempotency_key IS NOT NULL THEN v_existing := public.check_idempotency(p_idempotency_key, 'update_order_items'); IF v_existing IS NOT NULL THEN RETURN v_existing; END IF; END IF;`" and it returns before the FOR UPDATE lock, the ORDER_ITEM_MISMATCH check, and the delegation to _update_order_items_impl at :85-87.
2. The DB genuinely does not enforce payload binding here (checked, not "couldn't find"): grep of every migration defining the function (`grep -n "FUNCTION public.update_order_items"`) shows the last redefinition is 20260714221000; the only later files naming it (20260716120112, 20260721014858, 20260721223817) mention it in comments only. The current shared helper public.check_idempotency (latest definition supabase/migrations/20260714230000_gauntlet_core_guards.sql:5-52) compares only operation: ":40-43 `IF FOUND AND v_existing.operation IS DISTINCT FROM p_operation THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'IDEMPOTENCY_CROSS_OP_KEY_REUSE'`" then ":45-47 `IF FOUND THEN RETURN v_existing.result; END IF;`". No request_fingerprint/IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH/IDEMPOTENCY_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH migration names update_order_items. The impl writes its receipt only on commit (20260617123503_refresh_item_profit_on_sameproduct_order_edit.sql:317-318 `PERFORM save_idempotency(p_idempotency_key, 'update_order_items', v_result);`), so replay implies a real prior commit.
3. Not previously documented: no hit for "update_order_items" in docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md or docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md, and the 2026-08-06 section-06 idempotency refresh lists 1 HIGH/3 MED/3 LOW none of which is this RPC.

What is refuted / corrected:
a. The failure scenario's central step — "User re-opens the editor … clicks Save again. The same key is sent" — is wrong. src/pages/OrderDetail.tsx:1159 resets the key on entering edit mode: `onClick={() => { updateOrderIdem.resetKey(); setEditing(true); }}`. Re-opening the editor always mints a new key, so that path cannot replay.
b. The only reachable path is narrower: the save fails (lost response after commit), runCriticalAction (src/lib/criticalAction.ts:46-49) only toasts and leaves `editing` true, the user edits a value in the still-open editor and clicks Save Changes again (OrderDetail.tsx:1148). Then getKey() (src/hooks/useIdempotencyKey.ts:29-38, ref keyed only by [operation, userId]) returns the same key and the wrapper replays.
c. Impact is smaller than "silently discarded": after the replayed success toast the handler runs `fetchOrder()` (OrderDetail.tsx:527), which repaints items from the DB, so the un-applied edit is visible on screen immediately. Nothing incorrect is written to money or inventory; the defect is a false "Order updated" confirmation plus a lost edit intent — the same class the codebase already fixed for price_order with a payload-hash reset (OrderDetail.tsx:1022-1040, "editing a price and resubmitting would replay the SAME key … silently discarding the edited prices") and for NewOrder's rushOrderIdem. update_order_items has no such payload-change reset (updateOrderIdem appears only at OrderDetail.tsx:61, 501, 523, 1159).

Net: real gap, correct root cause, wrong reproduction step, MED not HIGH.

confirmed.title: Orders and invoices have no row-version stale-write guard — quotes/customers equivalents were never extended; two office users get last-write-wins
confirmed.detail: Checked the migrations: 20260730235031 adds row_version columns and bump triggers to exactly public.quotes and public.customers; no migration adds row_version (or any expected-version parameter) to orders, order_items, invoices, or invoice_items (`grep -rn "ADD COLUMN.*row_version" supabase/migrations` returns only the two 20260730235031 lines). update_order_items and save_invoice take row locks (serialization) but perform whole-collection replaces with no conflict detection, so the second writer wins silently. This is the direct answer to the row-version-equivalents question: THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE stale-write protection on orders/invoices (verified in migrations), and I did not find a settled decision excluding them — DECISION_LOG.md has zero row-version/stale/last-write entries about orders or invoices (grep), and KNOWN_ISSUES describes the 20260730 guard as closing the exposure only 'for whole-record save_quote and save_customer updates'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two office users open the same order's item editor. User A corrects a price and saves; user B (still holding the pre-edit rows) saves a quantity change seconds later. update_order_items locks and rewrites every supplied line from B's stale snapshot — A's price correction is silently reverted, affecting invoice totals and commission profit downstream. Identical exposure for two users editing the same draft invoice via save_invoice (its 20260803 fingerprint binds retries of one client's key, but does nothing across two different users' keys).
confirmed.evidence: 20260730235031:10-13: `ALTER TABLE public.quotes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS row_version…; ALTER TABLE public.customers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS row_version…` — the only two tables. 20260714221000:42: `PERFORM 1 FROM public.orders WHERE id = p_order_id FOR UPDATE;` — lock only, no version compare anywhere in the wrapper or its call into `_update_order_items_impl`.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED — every load-bearing claim verified independently; no refutation angle held.

(1) DB-level absence verified two ways, not one. 20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql:11-13 adds row_version to exactly public.quotes and public.customers. Beyond the reviewer's migration grep, live state agrees: .claude/schema-registry.json lists row_version under /columns/ only for customers, quotes, and pricing_workbook_export_rows — never orders, order_items, invoices, or invoice_items. So this is genuinely "the DB does not enforce X", not "I couldn't find where X is enforced".

(2) No later migration supersedes either path. Latest update_order_items is the 20260714221000 wrapper; lines 42-68 quoted accurately ("PERFORM 1 FROM public.orders WHERE id = p_order_id FOR UPDATE;" plus "FOR UPDATE OF oi"). Its only content-ish check is ORDER_ITEM_MISMATCH (lines 55-57), which asserts supplied ids belong to p_order_id — it never compares a field value to a client baseline. Latest save_invoice is 20260803010917:33; its fingerprint is gated behind "SELECT * FROM idempotency_keys WHERE idempotency_key = p_idempotency_key", so two users with two different keys never see each other's receipt. confirmed.title: allocate_payment allocation_sets version assignment is check-then-act — concurrent payments for one customer abort with a raw unique-constraint error
confirmed.detail: allocate_payment computes the next allocation-set version with `SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 … WHERE entity_type='payment' AND entity_id = p_customer_id` and then INSERTs. Nothing serializes two concurrent payments for the same customer before this read (the advisory/UNIQUE idempotency claim serializes only same-key retries; different users use different keys; no customer-row lock or per-customer advisory lock is taken before the MAX read — invoice rows are locked later, and two payments to different invoices of one customer share no row lock at all). The UNIQUE (entity_type, entity_id, version) constraint makes the race fail closed rather than corrupt: the loser blocks on the winner's index entry and then raises 23505.
confirmed.failure_scenario: AR clerk and a sales rep both record payments for the same farm within the same moment (different invoices, different keys). Both read MAX(version)=N; both INSERT version N+1; the second transaction aborts with 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "allocation_sets_entity_type_entity_id_version_key"' — a raw Postgres error surfaced to the user on the money path with no retry guidance; the entire payment (allocations, prepay) is rolled back and must be re-entered.
confirmed.evidence: 20260713060300:139-141: `SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 INTO v_next_version\n  FROM allocation_sets WHERE entity_type = 'payment' AND entity_id = p_customer_id;` then :142-152 INSERT. 20260213100000:116: `UNIQUE (entity_type, entity_id, version)`.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED. Code citations are accurate and no missed enforcement mechanism exists. (1) 20260713060300_harden_allocate_payment_idempotency.sql is the latest on-disk definition of allocate_payment — the three later migrations naming it (20260716120112_gauntlet_money_workflows.sql, 20260716160000_fix_idempotency_committed_replay_guard.sql, 20260718203206_retire_legacy_record_invoice_payment.sql) redefine save_invoice/get_customer_statement/_guard_idempotency_key_insert/record_invoice_payment, not allocate_payment. (2) The check-then-act is verbatim as quoted at :139-152. (3) The DB does not enforce serialization — checked, not merely unfound: the only customers read is `SELECT farm_name INTO v_customer_name FROM customers WHERE id = p_customer_id;` at :133 with NO `FOR UPDATE`; no pg_advisory lock anywhere in the body; the invoice `FOR UPDATE` at :164 comes after the INSERT and two payments to different invoices of one customer share no row lock. The per-customer lock existed historically (20260222200000_fix_allocate_payment_double_count.sql:59 and 20260223200000_payment_allocation.sql:59: `SELECT * INTO v_cust FROM customers WHERE id = p_customer_id FOR UPDATE;`) and was dropped when 20260316200001_fix_allocate_payment_missing_columns.sql introduced the MAX(version) scheme (MAX read at :64, no customers select at all); never restored. (4) UNIQUE (entity_type, entity_id, version) at 20260213100000_phase2_billing_architecture.sql:116 is still live — no migration drops it; 20260316200000 drops only allocation_sets_entity_type_check. 20260316200001's own header records this constraint firing in production before ("allocation_sets version always defaulted to 1, causing unique constraint violation on 2nd payment"). (5) trg_enforce_allocation_not_over_payment (20260616121105:34-37) is a value-only BEFORE-row check and takes no lock. (6) Not documented in docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md, the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline, or any docs/audits/gauntlet/*.md (no hit for MAX(version)/next_version/allocate_payment race).

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING. (a) The evidence claim "a raw Postgres error surfaced to the user" is factually wrong: both UI callers pass the error through sanitizeError (src/pages/PaymentAllocation.tsx:307, src/pages/InvoiceDetail.tsx:1049) and src/lib/errorSanitizer.ts:8-9 maps /duplicate key value violates unique constraint "[^"]+"/i to 'A record with this information already exists'. This does not reduce severity — it supports MED: on a payment screen that wording reads as "this payment was already recorded", so an AR clerk may believe the payment posted and never re-enter it (fail-closed abort becomes a silently missing payment). Recovery is otherwise one click: resetKey() runs only on success, so a resubmit reuses the same idempotency key, and the winner's claim row rolled back with its transaction, so the retry re-claims and succeeds. (b) The race window is wider than the finding states: the winner holds its uncommitted UNIQUE index entry from the INSERT at :142 through the invoice loop, prepay insert, activity_feed and financial_audit_log writes until COMMIT, so any second payment for the same customer that merely STARTS during that whole body still reads MAX(version)=N (the uncommitted row is invisible), then blocks and raises 23505.

Severity MED confirmed: fails closed with no money corruption, but sits on the cash-application path with a misleading user-facing message.

confirmed.title: QuoteBuilder failed-convert recovery writes quotes.status directly; the DB transition enforcer allows accepted→sent unconditionally, so a convert race can flip a converted quote back to 'sent'
confirmed.detail: After a failed convert RPC, the error path re-reads status and — when it is not 'accepted' — writes `supabase.from('quotes').update({ status: revertTo })` directly (bypassing revert_quote_status, which is the RPC that refuses reverting an accepted quote that has an order). Checked the migrations: the trigger _enforce_quote_status_transition permits `accepted → sent` with no orders-exist check (the orders-exist refusal exists only inside revert_quote_status), so the DB does not enforce the converted-quote invariant for direct writes. The window is the gap between the recovery read (~line 2625) and the update (2688): a convert committed from another tab in that gap makes this tab overwrite 'accepted' with 'sent' on a quote that now has an order and a fully-drawn ledger. Downstream damage is bounded: re-convert returns already_converted (draws guard), and the row_version bump invalidates other editors — but the quote shows 'sent' while its order exists, which QuoteBuilder's own comment at 2696-2700 treats as a manual-fix state.
confirmed.failure_scenario: User A's convert fails on a transient error; simultaneously user B (or A's second tab) converts the same quote successfully. A's recovery read raced ahead of B's commit (returned 'sent'), then A's direct update lands after B's commit, flipping the converted quote from accepted back to sent. Staff now see an open 'sent' booking that is actually fully drawn with a live order; conversion attempts return 'already_converted' info toasts, and the status must be fixed by hand.
confirmed.evidence: QuoteBuilder.tsx:2688: `const revertResult = await supabase.from('quotes').update({ status: revertTo }).eq('id', savedId).select('*');` — 20260706030000:103 in _enforce_quote_status_transition: `OR (OLD.status = 'accepted' AND NEW.status = 'sent')` with no accompanying EXISTS(orders) condition (the enforcer body contains no reference to the orders table).

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED — every load-bearing claim verified against current source and the full migration chain; no superseding enforcement found.

1) The direct write exists as quoted. src/pages/QuoteBuilder.tsx:2688 — `const revertResult = await supabase.from('quotes').update({ status: revertTo }).eq('id', savedId).select('*');`. It is preceded by the recovery read at :2613-2619 (`.from('quotes').select('status').eq('id', savedId).maybeSingle()`), the accepted-branch early return at :2625-2655, and the null-status early return at :2657-2664. `revertTo` is computed at :2685 from React state, not from `liveQuoteStatus`. The update carries NO `row_version`/status predicate — only `.eq('id', savedId)` — so it is a blind last-writer-wins write. The read→write window is real and unguarded.

2) The DB does NOT enforce the invariant (checked the migrations, not merely "couldn't find it"). `_enforce_quote_status_transition` is last redefined in supabase/migrations/20260706030000_closed_short_booking_closure.sql:74-121 — I confirmed by grep that this is the newest of the 11 migrations touching that function (20260228300000, 20260311200000, 20260319000000, 20260416100000, 20260511120000, 20260608154245, 20260610185806, 20260616204400, 20260702131000, 20260703200000, 20260706030000), and no later migration drops or replaces trigger `enforce_quote_status_transition` on quotes. Its body contains `OR (OLD.status = 'accepted' AND NEW.status = 'sent')` with no accompanying condition; the only `EXISTS` in the function targets `jobs` and is gated on `NEW.status = 'closed_short'`. There is no reference to `orders` anywhere in the function.

3) No other trigger closes the gap. The only other status trigger on quotes is `trg_enforce_quote_terminal_not_drawn` (20260614151956:50, body updated 20260616115308), which fires only when `OLD.status IN ('sent','revised') AND NEW.status IN ('declined','cancelled','expired')` — OLD='accepted' misses it entirely. `enforce_quote_accepted_fully_drawn` was DROPPED (20260610181612:292). `release_holds_on_quote_status_change` only acts when NEW is terminal, so it no-ops on accepted→sent.

4) The RPC the write bypasses does enforce it. `revert_quote_status` (20260718232157_harden_quote_reopen_history_guards.sql) refuses with `'Cannot revert accepted quote % — an active (non-cancelled) order exists from it'` and `QUOTE_REOPEN_HAS_ORDER_HISTORY`, and additionally zeroes `quote_product_draws` and rebuilds planned holds via `create_planned_holds` — none of which the direct write does.

5) The write is permitted at the RLS layer: `CREATE POLICY "quotes_update" ON quotes FOR UPDATE TO authenticated USING (is_admin() OR (is_sales_rep() AND created_by = (select auth.uid())))` (20260206174345_fix_security_and_performance_issues.sql:369-377); quotes was NOT included in the direct-DML revoke of 20260730235031 (which revokes only on quote_sections/quote_items/customer_addresses).

6) Not in the baseline. docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04… contains one finding (HIGH — Bulk Order Import bypassing the order lifecycle); it never mentions revert/accepted→sent or this recovery path. KNOWN_ISSUES.md has no entry for it — its nearest text (line 216) concerns client-side row-version token *adoption* on direct lifecycle writes, not a missing predicate on this write nor the DB's permissive accepted→sent edge.

Severity stays LOW, and two facts argue against raising it: (a) reachability is genuinely narrow — it needs A's convert to fail transiently (a lost-response-after-commit lands in the accepted branch at :2625 instead) AND B's convert to commit inside a single round trip between :2619 and :2688; (b) there is a post-hoc detector the reviewer did not credit — `applyDirectQuoteMutationRowVersion` (QuoteBuilder.tsx:697-718) sees the jumped token and raises "another edit may have completed at the same time… reload before saving, revising, or converting it", so the operator is warned even though the bad row is already committed. Two corrections/additions to the writeup: the read is at :2613-2619 (":2625" is the accepted-status check, not the read), and the unmentioned extra damage is that a planned booking flipped back to 'sent' this way keeps the holds released at accept time with no `create_planned_holds` rebuild — the direct write skips that half of `revert_quote_status` too.

confirmed.title: Assigned driver can complete a delivery by direct table UPDATE, bypassing complete_delivery's inventory, order-fulfillment, and invoice effects
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:83-93 (del_update policy); supabase/baselines/20260727174805_acl_lockdown.sql:174 (authenticated UPDATE grant on deliveries); baseline public_schema.sql line 3871 (_enforce_delivery_status_transition); baseline public_schema.sql line 2081 (_complete_delivery_authorized_impl)
confirmed.detail: The `del_update` RLS policy lets the assigned driver UPDATE a delivery whose OLD status is 'in_progress' or 'completed', and its WITH CHECK permits a NEW status in the same set. `authenticated` holds a table-level UPDATE grant on `public.deliveries`. The only BEFORE UPDATE OF status trigger, `_enforce_delivery_status_transition`, explicitly allows `in_progress -> completed`. `guard_completed_delivery_signature` only requires a non-blank `signed_by`, which the caller supplies. I checked every trigger on `public.deliveries` in the DR baseline (enforce_delivery_status_transition, trg_enforce_delivery_accounting_period, trg_guard_completed_delivery_signature, trg_delivery_status_change, guard_delivery_delete) — none performs the work the RPC does. Therefore: THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE that a delivery reaches 'completed' only through `complete_delivery()`. All of the completion side-effects live inside `_complete_delivery_authorized_impl`: `UPDATE delivery_items SET quantity_delivered`, `UPDATE order_items SET ...`, `INSERT INTO inventory_transactions`, `UPDATE inventory SET`, `UPDATE orders SET` (fulfilment status), `INSERT INTO invoices` + `invoice_items`, and `INSERT INTO financial_audit_log`. A direct PostgREST `PATCH /rest/v1/deliveries?id=eq.<id>` with `{"status":"completed","signed_by":"x"}` from the assigned driver's own JWT produces a completed delivery with no inventory decrement, no order progression, no invoice, and no financial audit row. The driver write path to this table is live and used today (src/pages/FieldStop.tsx:351 updates `deliveries.signature_url` directly), so nothing about the driver holding UPDATE here is theoretical.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver assigned to delivery D (status 'in_progress') sends PATCH /rest/v1/deliveries?id=eq.D with {"status":"completed","signed_by":"J. Doe"} using their own session token. RLS passes (assigned_driver = auth.uid(), old and new status both in the allowed set), the transition trigger passes, the signature guard passes. Result: delivery shows completed; on-hand inventory is never decremented; order_items.quantity_delivered stays 0 so the order never advances to partially_fulfilled/fulfilled; no invoice is generated so the customer is never billed; no financial_audit_log row exists. Net Position reports stock that has physically left the yard as available, and the load is delivered free.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED on the facts; severity corrected BLOCKER -> HIGH.

Independent verification (I decompressed the DR baseline `supabase/baselines/20260727174805_public_schema.sql.br` and re-derived every object rather than trusting the reviewer's citations):

1. Policy is current, not superseded. `del_update` in `supabase/migrations/20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:83-93` is reproduced verbatim in the baseline at `public_schema.sql:65825`: `USING ((is_admin() OR is_sales_rep() OR ((assigned_driver = (SELECT auth.uid())) AND (status = ANY (ARRAY['in_progress','completed'])))))` with an identical WITH CHECK. I grepped every migration timestamped after the baseline (20260727231652 through 20260807220323) for policy/grant/trigger changes on `deliveries` — zero hits. Nothing supersedes it.

2. Grant is table-level, not column-level. `supabase/baselines/20260727174805_acl_lockdown.sql:174` — `GRANT DELETE, INSERT, MAINTAIN, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE ON TABLE public.deliveries TO authenticated;` and baseline `public_schema.sql:73758` `GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."deliveries" TO "authenticated"`. No column list restricts the driver to signature columns — the old policy name `del_driver_signature_only` (dropped at 20260511060000:81) was aspirational; RLS cannot restrict columns.

3. Trigger inventory is complete and none does the RPC's work. Baseline `CREATE TRIGGER` lines on `public.deliveries`: `enforce_delivery_status_transition` (60343), `guard_delivery_delete` (60413), `trg_delivery_status_change` (60784), `trg_enforce_delivery_accounting_period` (60798), `trg_guard_completed_delivery_signature` (60847). I read all four relevant bodies:
   - `_enforce_delivery_status_transition` (public_schema.sql:3871) explicitly permits `OLD.status = 'in_progress' AND NEW.status IN ('completed','cancelled') THEN RETURN NEW;`
   - `guard_completed_delivery_signature` (32359) only raises `SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` when `signed_by` is blank — caller-supplied.
   - `enforce_delivery_accounting_period` (24456) only calls `check_period_open()`; passes for an open period.
   - `trg_delivery_status_change` (47400) only inserts an `activity_feed` row.
   No trigger touches inventory, order_items, invoices, or financial_audit_log, and none requires a "completed via RPC" marker (no `current_setting`/session-flag gate exists anywhere on this path).

4. No table constraint blocks it. `CREATE TABLE public.deliveries` has only `deliveries_issue_type_check`, `deliveries_priority_check`, `deliveries_status_check` (which lists 'completed' as legal); `completed_at` is nullable with no status-conditional CHECK. So `{"status":"completed","signed_by":"x"}` alone satisfies every DB check.

Conclusion on mechanism: this is genuinely "THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE that completion routes through complete_delivery" — not "I could not find the enforcement." I looked for it and it is absent.

Not previously documented. `docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` has no entry for `del_update`/`assigned_driver`/delivery-status direct writes (grep returned nothing). The 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline contains a single HIGH about Bulk Order Import and nothing about deliveries. The nearest prior coverage actively *misses* this: `docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-07-26-section-04-...:87` records "Skipping delivery confirm -> complete: refuted" reasoning only from the RPC path, and `docs/audits/2026-07-15-graph-workflow-analysis.md:111` says "inspected UI paths call confirm_delivery before complete_delivery; no bypass was confirmed" — both are UI/RPC-path statements, neither examines the table-write surface. The project has closed this exact class elsewhere (KNOWN_ISSUES.md:216 removes direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `quote_sections`/`quote_items`/`customer_addresses` from browser roles), which confirms it is treated as a real defect rather than accepted design — deliveries was simply not covered.

Severity correction to HIGH, on three grounds the finding overstates:
(a) Not reachable from the app. I grepped every frontend write to the table: only `src/pages/FieldStop.tsx:351` `.update({ signature_url: filePath })`. No code path in `src/` sets `deliveries.status` directly, so this cannot fire accidentally — it requires a deliberate hand-crafted PostgREST call.
(b) Not a privilege escalation. `supabase/migrations/20260716173342_authorize_delivery_before_replay.sql:80-85` authorizes `v_actor_role = 'driver' AND v_actor = v_delivery.assigned_driver` to call `complete_delivery`. No REVOKE of these in any later migration (grep of all REVOKE statements returns nothing touching orders/order_items tables).

(3) THE DB GENUINELY DOES NOT ENFORCE CONFIRMED-ONLY ON INSERT — this is a checked-the-migrations claim, not a could-not-find claim. Complete trigger set on orders in the live dump: enforce_order_status_transition (:60371, BEFORE UPDATE OF status), guard_order_customer_source_lineage (BEFORE UPDATE OF customer_id), guard_order_delete (:60455, BEFORE DELETE), guard_order_delivered_activity_cancel (BEFORE UPDATE OF status, deleted_at), trg_order_status_change (AFTER UPDATE), trg_stamp_commission_split_recipient_ids (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF commission_split). Not one constrains status on INSERT. orders_status_check at public_schema.sql:53614 permits confirmed/partially_fulfilled/fulfilled/cancelled/voided. Only THREE CREATE TRIGGER statements exist across every post-baseline migration (20260807215532 trg_guard_profile_role_lock; 20260730235031 quotes_bump_row_version and customers_bump_row_version) — none on orders or order_items.

(4) THE SECTION-4 REMEDIATION DOES NOT REACH THIS PATH. 20260805211951_harden_bulk_order_import_lifecycle.sql contains zero CREATE TRIGGER, zero CREATE POLICY, and zero table-level GRANT/REVOKE — its only ACL statements are REVOKE/GRANT EXECUTE on the RPC at :289 and :293. The 2026-08-05 gauntlet doc scopes its HIGH strictly to bulk_import_order and even corroborates the underlying gap: "Live `orders_status_check` permits partial and terminal statuses, so the database CHECK did not reject the structurally inconsistent rows." The raw-table path is a distinct, unremediated instance of the same defect class.

(5) NOT PREVIOUSLY DOCUMENTED. Zero hits for orders_insert/oitems_insert across all of docs/ and .claude/. No KNOWN_ISSUES entry, no accepted-residual note, no DECISION_LOG entry covering direct-table order writes.

(6) FAILURE SCENARIO IS REACHABLE. orders requires only order_number (text NOT NULL) and customer_id; status defaults to confirmed but is freely settable within the CHECK. is_sales_rep() (public_schema.sql) requires only role='sales_rep' AND is_active=true, so any active rep's own JWT satisfies the WITH CHECK. The canonical effects the reviewer lists live only inside create_direct_order (20260614142939:172-205) as function body, not as triggers, so a direct insert produces none of them.

TWO POINTS THAT STRENGTHEN THE FINDING BEYOND WHAT THE REVIEWER CLAIMED:
(a) Genuine RLS boundary crossing, not merely a lifecycle gap. orders_update (public_schema.sql:67480) and oitems_update (:67378) are ADMIN-ONLY — `FOR UPDATE TO "authenticated" USING ("public"."is_admin"()) WITH CHECK ("public"."is_admin"())`. Yet trg_recalc_order_totals is SECURITY DEFINER and executes `UPDATE orders SET total_price = ..., total_cost = ..., total_profit = ..., total_margin_pct = ...` on the parent. A sales rep therefore drives a privileged rewrite of an orders row they are explicitly denied UPDATE on, by inserting an order_items row — and oitems_insert has no parent-ownership or terminal-status predicate, while orders_select/oitems_select let any rep see every order, so target order_ids are trivially discoverable.
(b) The path is entirely UI-unreachable, so revocation is zero-cost. Zero .insert() calls against orders or order_items anywhere in src/ or supabase/functions/; NewOrder.tsx:516 uses supabase.rpc('create_direct_order', ...). The repo already set this exact precedent in 20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard, which stripped direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on quote_sections/quote_items/customer_addresses from normal browser roles for the same reason (KNOWN_ISSUES:216).

MINOR EVIDENCE ERRORS, NON-LOAD-BEARING: the reviewer's trigger list omits trg_snapshot_order_item_cost (public_schema.sql:61099, BEFORE INSERT ON order_items — only fills cost_at_time_cents from products.current_cost, constrains nothing) and guard_order_item_delivery_lineage (BEFORE UPDATE OF order_id, product_id), and names the delete trigger _guard_order_delete when the trigger is guard_order_delete (the function is _guard_order_delete). Neither changes the conclusion.

SEVERITY: HIGH sustained. It requires an authenticated active sales rep deliberately calling PostgREST outside the app rather than an ordinary UI action, which argues for MED under a strict honest-mistake threat model. But this repo has consistently rated direct-PostgREST-reachable defects as serious (KNOWN_ISSUES 0d profile_public_view RLS bypass; the SECDEF pricing reads reachable via direct /rpc/ at KNOWN_ISSUES:682), and the admin-only-UPDATE bypass in (a) is a real privilege-boundary violation on top of the lifecycle gap. Consequences are money- and inventory-bearing: unreserved stock feeding oversell through Net Position, missing commission liability, no activity_feed audit record, impossible fulfilled-with-zero-delivered state, and cross-rep desynchronisation of order profit from billed invoice revenue.

The function derives `v_actor := auth.uid()` and gates on `is_admin() OR is_sales_rep()`, but never requires `p_salesman_id = v_actor` and never requires the supplied uuid to be an active sales_rep. `invoices.salesman_id` is not merely attribution: `invoices_select` grants full row read on `salesman_id = auth.uid()`, and `invoice_items_select` inherits it — and `invoice_items.cost_cents` / `invoices.total_cost_cents` are internal cost. The frontend always passes `profile.id` (OrderDetail.tsx:864,880), which is also a second, non-adversarial problem: any sales_rep pressing "Create Invoice" on another rep's order silently reassigns the invoice's salesman to themselves, moving `get_sales_detail_report`/`get_sales_summary_report` attribution. The standing `actor-forgery` predicate cannot catch this: it only considers argument names matching `^p_\w*by$|^p_actor|^p_user`, and `p_salesman_id` matches none of them.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sales_rep calls /rest/v1/rpc/create_invoice_from_order with p_salesman_id set to a driver's (or an entity_recipient's) uuid. In the everyday non-adversarial case, rep B invoices rep A's order from the UI and the invoice's salesman_id silently becomes B, shifting the sales reports and the read grant away from A.

confirmed.title: generate_order_number() and generate_quote_number() remain EXECUTE-able by anon and call nextval() — a logged-out visitor can burn the order and quote number sequences
confirmed.detail: Both functions are invoker-rights but call `nextval('order_number_seq')` / `nextval('quote_number_seq')`, which is a mutation, and `anon` holds `SELECT, UPDATE, USAGE` on sequences via the standing `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`. The 2026-07-28 hardening (`20260728231350_revoke_anon_execute_non_policy_functions`, KNOWN_ISSUES section 0c) explicitly identified the document-number allocators as "the actual live exposure" and revoked the six `next_*_number()` functions — it did not include these two, which are the allocators the order and quote creation RPCs actually use. I diffed the full set of 95 anon-EXECUTE grants in the DR baseline against the 43 revoked by the two 2026-07-28 migrations, and grepped every migration for a later revoke of either name: none exists. confirmed.failure_scenario: An unauthenticated visitor with the publishable anon key (embedded in the shipped bundle) loops POST /rest/v1/rpc/generate_order_number a few thousand times. `order_number_seq` advances with no order rows created. Zero-arg VOLATILE plpgsql returning text = PostgREST exposes it at `POST /rest/v1/rpc/...`.

4. The sequence privilege the reviewer asserts is actually stronger than claimed, and explicit. Not merely via `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` (that only covers future sequences) — `acl_lockdown.sql:407` and `:473` carry direct grants: `GRANT SELECT, UPDATE, USAGE ON SEQUENCE public.order_number_seq TO anon;` and the same for `quote_number_seq`. Invoker-rights + anon holding USAGE/UPDATE = `nextval()` succeeds as anon. This is the one place the reviewer's mechanism description is imprecise, and the imprecision is in the finding's disfavor, not its favor.

5. Not already documented. `docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:532-590` (section 0c) names exactly 40+3 functions and calls the six `next_*_number()` "the actual live exposure"; `generate_order_number`/`generate_quote_number` are absent from that section and from the whole file. `docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md` never mentions either name or anon function grants. No `docs/` or `.claude/` file tracks this as an open item. The reviewer's framing — residue of a class the project already closed — is accurate.

6. The callers claim is accurate. `generate_order_number()` is called by the live order-creation path including `20260702172500_layer2_convert_quote_to_order_job_aware.sql:155`, `20260614142939_create_direct_order_customer_po_param.sql:93`, `20260614144757_create_rush_order.sql:118`; `generate_quote_number()` by `20260609195843_strict_actor_quote_rpcs.sql:126,328` and `20260611211058_idempotency_operation_scope_sweep.sql:1113,2027`. WHY I LOWERED SEVERITY TO LOW. I tried to find a harder impact and could not:
- Both `orders.order_number` and `quotes.quote_number` are `"text" NOT NULL` (baseline public_schema), so an inflated `lpad(...,4,'0')` value cannot overflow a column and cause insert failures — no DoS on order creation.
- `CREATE SEQUENCE "public"."order_number_seq" START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1 NO MINVALUE NO MAXVALUE CACHE 1` — bigint ceiling 9.2e18, unreachable over HTTP, so no exhaustion failure mode.
- anon holds UPDATE on the sequences, which in principle permits `setval()` (rewinding into collisions with existing numbers would be genuinely bad), but `setval` lives in `pg_catalog`, is not in an exposed schema, and PostgREST will not route to it — so the only reachable primitive is monotonic advance.

No confidentiality of customer/money data, no record-integrity violation, no privilege escalation, one-line fix (`REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC, anon` on both, naming both grantees per the section-0c mechanics note). That is LOW. The counter-argument for holding MED is class parity — the six `next_*_number()` siblings are mechanically identical and the project revoked them as a security fix — which is a consistency argument for fixing it, not evidence of higher impact.

CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE STRENGTH: this is an offline determination. The strongest artifact available to me is the `20260727174805` DR baseline, which is a capture of live ACLs at that timestamp, plus an exhaustive read of the 29 post-baseline migrations. I did not query the live database. If any ACL change reached production through the Management API without a repo migration file, the conclusion about current live grants could differ; note that `docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:802-806` records that 654 live ledger versions have no matching repo file, so that channel demonstrably exists. Confirming with one read-only `has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.generate_order_number()', 'EXECUTE')` against live would close the gap.

confirmed.title: release_expired_quote_holds() is an ungated authenticated-callable SECURITY DEFINER mutator with no idempotency key, and the standing ungated-secdef-mutators predicate cannot see it

(b) `docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:261` and `:285` record the live sweep output as ungated-secdef-mutators = 1 allowlisted row — i.e. the function is genuinely absent from live sweep results, corroborating the miss against the real catalog, not just against a dump. (c) The predicate header documents only ONE known approximation (helper-gated functions); the alias gap is undocumented. (d) Authoring-time hooks do not cover it: `grep -n "SECURITY DEFINER|secdef|auth\.uid|require_admin|GRANT" .claude/hooks/sql-safety.mjs` returns nothing, and `.claude/hooks/idempotency-body-check.mjs:394` short-circuits with `if (!/p_idempotency_key\s+text/i.test(params)) continue;` — a new mutating RPC that simply omits the parameter is never inspected. Its own mutation test at :396 uses `\b(INSERT\s+INTO|UPDATE\s+|DELETE\s+FROM)\b`, which WOULD match an aliased UPDATE — direct proof the sweep predicate's `\S+\s+set` is an avoidable authoring defect, since the sibling guard in the same repo gets it right. (e) Neither the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline (line 77: "All 21 live invariant predicates: zero unallowlisted violations") nor KNOWN_ISSUES mentions predicate coverage limits — that "clean" is exactly the signal the blind spot produces.

CORRECTION 1 — the "ungated SECDEF mutator" half is a documented, deliberate disposition, not an undetected hole. `supabase/migrations/20260609203541_harden_maintenance_secdef_revoke_authenticated.sql:15-19` states verbatim: "NOT touched (explicitly justified, Codex #2/#3): log_failed_notification + release_expired_quote_holds are frontend-called (Dashboard.tsx / notificationTriggers.ts), already authenticated-only (anon revoked), and benign (write a failure-log row / release already-expired inventory holds). A hard auth.uid() gate would break their cron / service_role / Edge-function callers (auth.uid() is NULL there)". Two callers confirm the rationale: `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:329` (`supabase.rpc('release_expired_quote_holds')`) and the pg_cron schedule at `supabase/migrations/20260501140000_field_app_workflow_phase19.sql:47-51` (`$$SELECT public.release_expired_quote_holds()$$`, 6:15 AM UTC). The grant at `20260302200000_business_logic_enhancements.sql:1537` is still live — no later `REVOKE`/`CREATE OR REPLACE` touches it (grep over all migrations returns only line 1515). So the function's ungated state is a settled accepted risk; the REAL process defect is that this disposition lives in a migration comment and was never written into `allowlist.json`, so the sweep reads clean by accident rather than by decision. That is a narrower but still valid finding.

CORRECTION 2 — the second example is weaker than claimed. `settle_applied_record_acres` (`supabase/migrations/20260624181000_fix_applied_acres_integrity.sql:97-121`, body `UPDATE job_applied_records r SET applied_acres = ...`) is REVOKEd from PUBLIC and anon at :122-123 and is never explicitly GRANTed to `authenticated` anywhere in the migrations. Whether `has_function_privilege('authenticated', ...)` is true depends solely on Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` (referenced at `20260728231350_revoke_anon_execute_non_policy_functions.sql:11-13`). I did not verify live ACL, so this instance is unproven from source. It is also trigger-invoked only (`PERFORM settle_applied_record_acres(...)` at :151/:155), so even if callable it is a convergent recompute.

CORRECTION 3 — the generalization is overstated. "any future ungated mutator written with an alias will pass too" is false as written: `insert\s+into` and `delete\s+from` match regardless of aliasing, so only a function whose ENTIRE DML set is aliased UPDATEs is invisible. The reviewer's own hypothetical (`UPDATE orders o SET status = ...`) slips through only if that function performs no INSERT or DELETE anywhere in its body — real, but a narrower window than stated.

NET: the failure scenario can occur, the fix is a one-token regex change (`update\s+\S+\s+set` → `update\s+` or an alias-tolerant `update\s+\S+(\s+(as\s+)?\S+)?\s+set`) in two predicate files, plus an allowlist entry recording the 20260609203541 disposition. Severity MED sustained — no live exploit (the UPDATE converges to the same state a Dashboard load or the 6:15 UTC cron produces), but it is a verified hole in the standing detection gate that section-04 and the gauntlet report as clean.

confirmed.title: Direct UPDATE of quotes.is_planned is unguarded — planned inventory holds desynchronise because holds are only reconciled on a status change
confirmed.location: supabase/migrations/20260206174345_fix_security_and_performance_issues.sql:369 (quotes_update); supabase/baselines/20260727174805_acl_lockdown.sql:497 (authenticated UPDATE grant on quotes); baseline public_schema.sql line 39463 (release_holds_on_quote_status_change); supabase/migrations/20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql:82-84
confirmed.detail: The 2026-07-30 row-version work deliberately revoked direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from browser roles on `quote_sections`, `quote_items` and `customer_addresses`, routing those writes through `save_quote`. It did not do the same for the parent `quotes` table: `authenticated` still holds full DML there, and `quotes_update` lets an admin or the owning sales_rep write any column directly. Planned inventory holds are created and unwound inside `save_quote` / `_sync_planned_holds`; the only trigger that touches `inventory_holds` from the quotes table is `trg_release_holds_on_quote_status`, which fires `AFTER UPDATE OF status` only. I enumerated every trigger on `public.quotes` in the DR baseline (enforce_quote_accepted_fully_drawn, _enforce_quote_status_transition, trg_enforce_quote_terminal_not_drawn, trg_release_holds_on_quote_status, trg_stamp_commission_split_recipient_ids, trg_validate_quote_commission_split, plus the post-baseline quotes_bump_row_version) — none is on `is_planned`. THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE hold/flag coherence for a direct `is_planned` write.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sales_rep sends PATCH /rest/v1/quotes?id=eq.<their quote> with {"is_planned": false}. RLS passes (they are created_by), no trigger fires on that column, and the quote's active `inventory_holds` rows survive with `is_planned = false` — product stays reserved against a quote that is no longer a plan, understating Net Position indefinitely. The inverse write ({"is_planned": true}) marks the quote as planned with no holds created at all, so the same units are offered for sale twice.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED on mechanism; two impact claims are wrong and are corrected below. Severity stays MED.

VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE
1. Grant is real and never revoked. supabase/baselines/20260727174805_acl_lockdown.sql:497 — "GRANT DELETE, INSERT, MAINTAIN, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE ON TABLE public.quotes TO authenticated;". I searched every file under supabase/migrations/ for a later "REVOKE ... ON [TABLE] public.quotes": zero hits. The 2026-07-30 lockdown (supabase/migrations/20260730235031_quote_customer_row_version_guard.sql:80-82) revokes only quote_sections, quote_items, customer_addresses — public.quotes is absent, as claimed.
2. Policy is real. supabase/migrations/20260206174345_fix_security_and_performance_issues.sql:369-377 defines quotes_update with USING/WITH CHECK = is_admin() OR (is_sales_rep() AND created_by = auth.uid()); the live shape matches the DR baseline (public_schema.sql:68045). No column-level restriction anywhere.
3. Trigger enumeration is correct and complete. Grepping the decompressed baseline for triggers ON "public"."quotes" returns exactly six (public_schema.sql:60385, 60392, 60812, 61057, 61127, 61225): four are "BEFORE/AFTER UPDATE OF status", two are "OF commission_split". The only post-baseline CREATE TRIGGER on quotes across all migrations is quotes_bump_row_version (20260730235031:64), "BEFORE UPDATE ... EXECUTE FUNCTION public.bump_record_row_version()", whose body is only "NEW.row_version := OLD.row_version + 1" — it does not block or reconcile anything. THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE is_planned/hold coherence on a direct write; this is a migration-verified negative, not a failure to find.
4. Reconciliation really is RPC-only. public._sync_planned_holds (public_schema.sql:11003) self-gates on "IF NOT v_quote.is_planned OR v_quote.status NOT IN ('draft','sent','revised') THEN ... release" and its own comment says it "additionally covers is_planned switched off without a status change" (11026-11027) — but every call site is a function body (save_quote 11243, restore_quote_version 21096, cancel/order paths 910/1631/12114), never a trigger. release_holds_on_quote_status_change (39463) keys on status exactly as quoted.
5. Not previously documented. Zero occurrences of "is_planned" in docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md or in any file under docs/audits/gauntlet/. Note the cited baseline docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md DOES NOT EXIST in this checkout (latest section-04 refreshes are 2026-07-22 and 2026-07-26); neither mentions is_planned.

IMPACT CORRECTIONS (the reviewer's failure_scenario is partly wrong)
A. "understating Net Position" is inaccurate as written. get_inventory_position computes "(b.quantity_available - b.quantity_prebooked + COALESCE(oo.qty, 0)) AS net_position" (public_schema.sql:29429) — holds are NOT subtracted from net_position; holds_qty is a separate reported column. The real capacity harm is elsewhere and is genuine: create_inventory_hold derives "v_todays_free := quantity_available - quantity_prebooked - v_active_holds" from all is_active holds with no quote join (public_schema.sql:19985-19998, raises INSUFFICIENT_HOLD_INVENTORY), and the job shortfall check subtracts "SUM(h.quantity) FROM inventory_holds h WHERE ... is_active" the same way (10826-10829). A stale hold does consume real capacity there.
B. "the same units are offered for sale twice" on an is_planned=false→true flip is REFUTED for the main surface. get_inventory_position's planned_quotes CTE reads the booking straight from quote_items — "WHERE q.is_planned = true AND q.status IN ('draft','sent','revised')" (public_schema.sql:29341) — and reports "booked − linked_hold − order_drawn − job_drawn" as planned_qty (29332-29366). With no holds created, linked_hold = 0, so the FULL booking still surfaces as planned demand; that is the explicit "no double count" design. The gap is narrower: get_inventory_forecast is hold-only (29236-29252) and the hold-aware free checks in (A) under-reserve.
C. "indefinitely" is overstated. Planned holds carry expires_at = needed_by_date + 14 days (_sync_planned_holds, public_schema.sql:11094), and every consumer filters "expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at >= CURRENT_DATE", so the stale hold ages out; it also self-heals on the next save_quote, which re-runs _sync_planned_holds.

HARM THE REVIEWER MISSED (argues MED, not LOW)
A direct PATCH of is_planned=false bypasses save_quote's explicit BOOKING_HAS_JOB_RESERVATION guard (public_schema.sql:43992-44005: "block unplanning a booking a scheduled job is still drawing from (Codex final push-gate P1 #1) ... reopening the full booking balance while the job still consumes the stock (double-count)"). Once is_planned is false, _sync_quote_job_reservations sets "v_planned_open := FOUND AND v_quote.is_planned AND ..." (11126-11128) and then unconditionally deletes non-consumed job draws (11144-11148) — i.e. the exact double-count that guard was written to prevent, reachable by a write path the guard does not cover. No detective control catches it either: the integrity sweep's stale_quote_hold alert keys on terminal STATUS only ("q.status IN ('declined','expired','cancelled','closed_by_application','closed_short')", public_schema.sql:40690-40694), and there is no is_planned predicate under scripts/db-invariant-sweeps/predicates/.

WHY NOT HIGHER THAN MED
Not reachable from the app: the only UI write of quotes.is_planned is the save_quote payload (src/pages/QuoteBuilder.tsx:1439); the direct .update() calls on quotes are status (QuoteBuilder.tsx:1731, 2688) and deleted_at (Quotes.tsx:409). Exploiting requires a hand-crafted PostgREST call by an authenticated admin/owning rep, the drift is bounded by hold expiry, and it self-heals on the next save_quote.

confirmed.title: global_search is an ungated SECURITY DEFINER reader that enumerates order, invoice and delivery numbers with customer names to every authenticated role
confirmed.detail: `global_search(p_query text, p_limit integer)` is `SECURITY DEFINER` with `EXECUTE` to `authenticated` and no auth or role test in the body. It reads `customers`, `orders`, `invoices`, `deliveries` and `products` under definer rights, so it bypasses `customers_select` (sales_rep scoped to `assigned_sales_rep`), `orders_select` (admin/sales_rep only), `invoices_select` and `del_select`. It returns identifiers and names, not amounts, so the direct disclosure is modest — but it hands a driver or applicator a working enumeration oracle for the customer uuids and invoice/order ids needed to exploit the ungated SECDEF readers above.
confirmed.evidence:
baseline public_schema.sql:32158 —
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."global_search"("p_query" "text", "p_limit" integer DEFAULT 5) RETURNS TABLE("entity_type" "text", "id" "uuid", "primary_text" "text", "secondary_text" "text")
    LANGUAGE "plpgsql" SECURITY DEFINER
    SET "search_path" TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
    AS $$
...
BEGIN
  IF length(trim(p_query)) < 2 THEN
    RETURN;
  END IF;

(first statement is the length check — no auth.uid(), is_admin(), is_sales_rep(), or profiles lookup)

    SELECT 'invoice'::text AS entity_type, i.id, i.invoice_number AS primary_text, COALESCE(c3.farm_name, '')::text
    FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN customers c3 ON c3.id = i.customer_id
    WHERE i.invoice_number ILIKE v_pattern
confirmed.failure_scenario: An applicator calls /rest/v1/rpc/global_search {"p_query":"a","p_limit":1000} and receives customer uuids and farm names for accounts they are assigned to none of, plus invoice and order ids. Those uuids are the input the ungated get_customer_year_end_summary / check_customer_credit_limit calls need, converting a name-only leak into a full financial read.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED. Every load-bearing claim checks out against current source, and I found no enforcement mechanism the reviewer missed.

1) Function shape is as claimed. supabase/migrations/20260404080000_fix_global_search_ilike_escape.sql:12-22 defines it `LANGUAGE plpgsql / SECURITY DEFINER / SET search_path = public, pg_temp`, and the first statement in the body is `IF length(trim(p_query)) < 2 THEN RETURN; END IF;` — no `auth.uid()`, `is_admin()`, `is_sales_rep()`, `is_active_profile()`, or profiles lookup anywhere in the body. The post-baseline dump agrees: decompressed supabase/baselines/20260727174805_public_schema.sql.br line 32158 carries the identical definition, so the baseline (2026-07-27) is the authoritative current shape.

2) No later migration supersedes it. `grep -rl global_search supabase/` returns only 20260404040100_global_search_rpc.sql, 20260404080000_fix_global_search_ilike_escape.sql, 20260529214355_revoke_anon_execute_on_report_dashboard_secdef.sql, 20260702170000 (a comment only), and the two baselines. Nothing after the 2026-07-27 baseline redefines the function or narrows its ACL. The one migration that touched its grants moved in the opposite direction of a fix: 20260529214355:100-101 `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC;` then `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO authenticated, service_role;` — that migration deliberately closed only the anon hole and preserved authenticated access ("so the logged-in app is unaffected", lines 15-18). The role-hardening wave of 2026-07-27/28 (broad_reads_require_active_profile, quote_and_rate_reads_office_only, secdef_pricing_reads_office_only, revoke_anon_execute_non_policy_functions) does not touch global_search. Baseline ACL confirms the live grant: supabase/baselines/20260727174805_acl_lockdown.sql:1216 `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.global_search(p_query text, p_limit integer) TO authenticated;` and public_schema.sql:71577.

3) The RLS bypass is real, not assumed — I checked the policies rather than assuming them. public_schema.sql:65607 `customers_select ... USING ((is_admin() OR (is_sales_rep() AND assigned_sales_rep = auth.uid()) OR (is_driver() AND EXISTS (...))))`; :67473 `orders_select ... USING ((is_admin() OR is_sales_rep()))`; :66652 `invoices_select ... USING ((is_admin() OR created_by = auth.uid() OR salesman_id = auth.uid()))`; :65818 `del_select ... USING ((is_admin() OR is_sales_rep() OR assigned_driver = auth.uid()))`. `grep -n "FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY" schema.sql` returns zero hits, so the definer (table owner) is exempt from all four — the bypass actually occurs, it is not merely theoretical.

4) The affected roles exist. .claude/schema-registry.json `profiles.role`: `["admin","sales_rep","driver","applicator","entity_recipient"]`. An applicator holds none of the branches in customers_select/orders_select, so global_search returns rows they can read by no other path. The exposure is live in the product, not just at the REST layer: src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:69 mounts `<CommandPalette open={paletteOpen} .../>` with no role gate.

5) The chained-escalation premise also checks out. Both named follow-on readers are still ungated SECDEF with authenticated EXECUTE: public_schema.sql:15495 `check_customer_credit_limit(p_customer_id uuid) ... SECURITY DEFINER` whose body opens with a bare `SELECT credit_limit_cents, farm_name ... FROM customers WHERE id = p_customer_id` (no auth test), granted at :70055; and :27329 `get_customer_year_end_summary(p_customer_id uuid, p_season integer) ... SECURITY DEFINER`, body opens `SELECT * INTO v_cust FROM customers WHERE id = p_customer_id`, granted at :71083. No migration after 2026-07-13 touches either. So the name-to-uuid oracle does feed a genuine financial read.

6) Not previously documented. `grep -i global_search` over docs/manual/*.md and docs/audits/gauntlet/*.md returns zero hits — it is absent from KNOWN_ISSUES.md and from the 2026-08-05 section-04 baseline. This is beyond the stated baseline.

Two minor corrections to the failure_scenario that do not change the substance: (a) `{"p_query":"a"}` returns nothing — the finding's own quoted `length(trim(p_query)) < 2` guard rejects it; the attack needs a 2+ character seed such as "aa" or "jo". (b) A single `%` wildcard dump is no longer possible — escaping metacharacters is exactly what the cited migration fixed (line 26, `v_escaped := regexp_replace(trim(p_query), '([%_\\])', ...)`), so this is two-character substring enumeration rather than a one-shot dump. `p_limit` is uncapped in the function (each branch is `LIMIT p_limit`) while the UI passes only 5 (src/components/ui/CommandPalette.tsx:250-251), so a direct REST call with p_limit=1000 works as described, and a few hundred bigram queries enumerate the active customer book.

The reviewer's "identifiers and names, not amounts" framing understates it: farm_name plus contact_name is customer PII, and the function bypasses four separate SELECT policies — including customers_select, which was deliberately written narrow — for a role class (applicator, entity_recipient) that has no customer read grant at all. Combined with the confirmed-still-ungated check_customer_credit_limit and get_customer_year_end_summary, this is the working first stage of a full financial read, and the palette is mounted for every role today. Still short of HIGH because the function itself returns no money values and the audience is authenticated staff rather than the public.

confirmed.title: Sales reps can insert deliveries directly, including in a terminal status, bypassing create_delivery_with_items' order-status, quantity and address-ownership validation
confirmed.detail: `del_insert` is `WITH CHECK (is_admin() OR is_sales_rep())` and `authenticated` holds INSERT on `public.deliveries`. The canonical creator `create_delivery_with_items` enforces that the parent order is `confirmed` or `partially_fulfilled` (`ORDER_NOT_SCHEDULABLE`), that the customer matches the order (`CUSTOMER_ORDER_MISMATCH`), that no order_item is duplicated, that scheduled quantities do not exceed the remaining order quantity, and that the delivery address belongs to that customer. None of those are triggers. The triggers on `deliveries` that do run on INSERT are `trg_enforce_delivery_accounting_period` (period-open only) and `trg_guard_completed_delivery_signature` (non-blank signed_by when status='completed'); `_enforce_delivery_status_transition` is BEFORE UPDATE OF status, so it never sees an INSERT. I found no BEFORE INSERT trigger restricting `deliveries.status` to 'scheduled'. THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE the RPC's preconditions on the direct-insert path.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sales_rep POSTs /rest/v1/deliveries with {"delivery_number":"D-9999","order_id":"<a cancelled order>","customer_id":"<a different customer>","status":"completed","signed_by":"x","scheduled_date":"2026-08-09"}. The row is accepted: the order-status gate, the customer/order coherence gate and the quantity gate all live in the RPC and are skipped. A 'completed' delivery now exists against a cancelled order for the wrong customer, with no inventory movement, no invoice, and no delivery_items — and the AFTER UPDATE completion machinery will never run for it because it was never updated into that state.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED as a real DB-enforcement gap, with two citation corrections. Verified against the decompressed live baseline (supabase/baselines/20260727174805_public_schema.sql.br), not merely against the migration the reviewer cited.

WHAT HOLDS (all verified, DB-does-not-enforce, not merely not-found):
1. Current effective policy: public_schema.sql:65717 — CREATE POLICY "del_insert" ON "public"."deliveries" FOR INSERT TO "authenticated" WITH CHECK (("public"."is_admin"() OR "public"."is_sales_rep"())). No created_by binding, no order/customer/status predicate.
2. Grant: acl_lockdown.sql:174 — GRANT DELETE, INSERT, MAINTAIN, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE ON TABLE public.deliveries TO authenticated. Verbatim as cited. (anon gets only MAINTAIN, SELECT at :173.)
3. No CHECK pins INSERT status: public_schema.sql:51677 — CONSTRAINT "deliveries_status_check" CHECK (("status" = ANY (ARRAY['scheduled','in_progress','completed','cancelled','voided']))). Column default 'scheduled' (:51653) is a default, not a constraint.
4. Trigger inventory on deliveries is exactly five (public_schema.sql:60343, 60413, 60784, 60798, 60847). Only two fire on INSERT and I read both bodies: guard_completed_delivery_signature only raises SIGNATURE_REQUIRED when status='completed' AND signed_by is blank; enforce_delivery_accounting_period's TG_OP='INSERT' branch only calls check_period_open() for status completed/voided. Neither checks order status, customer coherence, or quantity.
5. Reviewer is right that the transition guard cannot fire: :60343 — CREATE TRIGGER "enforce_delivery_status_transition" BEFORE UPDATE OF "status" ON "public"."deliveries". There is NO BEFORE INSERT status trigger.
6. All five gates are genuinely RPC-only (create_delivery_with_items, public_schema.sql:19431-19600): FORBIDDEN role check, CUSTOMER_ORDER_MISMATCH, ORDER_NOT_SCHEDULABLE (status NOT IN confirmed/partially_fulfilled), ADDRESS_CUSTOMER_MISMATCH, ITEM_DUPLICATE_IN_REQUEST, ITEM_ORDER_MISMATCH, and ITEM_OVER_REMAINING_INCL_ACTIVE. The RPC hardcodes status 'scheduled' on its own INSERT.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED TO OVERTURN IT:
- Later-migration supersession: newest migration touching deliveries policies is 20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql, which LOOSENS (drops the created_by binding). Nothing after it re-tightens.
- Post-baseline scan: every migration with timestamp > 20260727174805 mentioning deliveries (20260727231652, 20260730114102, 20260730124308, 20260730140808, 20260730235031, 20260803010917) uses deliveries only in read-only SELECT count(*)/NOT EXISTS. No new guard, policy, or trigger.
- Duplicate check: the 2026-08-05 gauntlet section-04 doc contains exactly one finding, 'HIGH — Bulk Order Import bypassed the canonical order lifecycle' (line 31) — unrelated. KNOWN_ISSUES.md does not cover deliveries direct-insert; the nearest entry (KNOWN_ISSUES.md:216) proposes revoking direct browser-role INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on quote_sections, quote_items, customer_addresses — deliveries is NOT in that list, and it is a candidate remediation, not applied. So the project's own stated fix direction matches this finding but has never reached this table.
- Threat-model exemption: the 'honest-mistake threat model' accepted residuals (KNOWN_ISSUES.md:1031, 1036, 1039) scope to agent proof-file self-attestation and shell/npm guard regexes — not to table grants or RLS, which this project actively hardens (20260727145843, 20260727174657, 20260727174805, 20260729125227).

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING (do not change the verdict):
(a) The location citation is WRONG. 20260210_fix_rls_critical_issues.sql:28-33 actually reads: CREATE POLICY "del_insert" ON deliveries FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (is_admin() OR (is_sales_rep() AND created_by = (select auth.uid()))). The reviewer's '...' elision hides this. The quoted policy body is really from supabase/migrations/20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:94-98, which DROPs the 20260210 version and removes the created_by binding. Correct location: 20260511060000_perf_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql:94-98 (+ baseline public_schema.sql:65717). The reviewer reached the right current-state conclusion via the wrong file.
(b) The failure-scenario payload is incomplete: deliveries.created_by is NOT NULL with no default (public_schema.sql:51659), so the literal POST shown fails. The attacker must add their own uid — trivial, non-material.

SEVERITY: keeping MED, neither raised nor lowered. Mitigations against raising: no frontend path direct-inserts into deliveries (grep of src/ for from('deliveries') + .insert returns zero; create_delivery_with_items and create_quick_delivery are the only creation paths), anon cannot INSERT, exploitation needs an authenticated admin/sales_rep deliberately hand-crafting a PostgREST call, and enforce_delivery_accounting_period DOES block a directly-inserted 'completed' row in a CLOSED period. Reasons against lowering to LOW: an open-period insert is fully unguarded, the resulting row corrupts inventory/AR reporting with no inventory movement and no invoice, the AFTER UPDATE completion machinery (trg_delivery_status_change) never runs for it, and a plausible non-terminal variant (direct insert at status='scheduled' plus delivery_items, which del_items_insert also permits to sales_rep) silently defeats the ITEM_OVER_REMAINING_INCL_ACTIVE quantity gate on a money/inventory-adjacent lifecycle table.

confirmed.title: Quotes list bulk-delete leaks inventory holds: soft-delete changes no status, so the hold-release trigger never fires and the reserved units stay counted forever
confirmed.detail:
`handleDelete` soft-deletes quotes with a raw `.update({ deleted_at })`. Its only guard is 'skip quotes with order/job draw-downs' (lines 387-406). A `sent`/`revised` planned booking with ZERO draws is deleted freely — and deletion changes no status, so nothing releases its `inventory_holds` rows.

This is a DB-enforcement gap I verified in the migrations, not a 'couldn't find it' claim:
- The release trigger is `AFTER UPDATE OF status ON quotes` and its body only fires `IF NEW.status IN ('accepted','declined','expired','cancelled','closed_by_application','closed_short') AND OLD.status NOT IN (...)`. A `deleted_at`-only UPDATE does not fire the `UPDATE OF status` trigger at all.

- Every free-stock reader sums `inventory_holds` with no join back to `quotes` and no deleted-quote filter, so the orphaned holds keep subtracting from Net Free forever.

Note `DELETABLE = ['draft','sent','revised']` (Quotes.tsx:32) is exactly the open-planned set that holds inventory, so this is the normal case, not an edge case.
