verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED as a real DB-enforcement gap, with two of the reviewer's supporting claims corrected (they overstate permanence and irrecoverability). Severity corrected HIGH -> MED.

WHAT I VERIFIED HOLDS UP (checked the migrations, not "couldn't find it"):

1. Write path is as quoted. src/pages/Quotes.tsx:407-412 `supabase.from('quotes').update({ deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() }).in('id', ids)` — a raw table UPDATE that names only `deleted_at`. The only guard (Quotes.tsx:385-402) queries `quote_product_draws` / `job_product_draws` for `quantity_drawn > 0`; there is no `is_planned` check, no hold check. `DELETABLE = ['draft','sent','revised']` (Quotes.tsx:32) is enforced only as row selectability (Quotes.tsx:323, 327) and is exactly the open-planned set that holds stock.

2. The release trigger genuinely cannot fire. Latest CREATE TRIGGER is supabase/migrations/20260312200000_business_logic_audit_fixes.sql:63-67 — `AFTER UPDATE OF status ON quotes`; I grepped every `CREATE TRIGGER ... ON quotes` in all 859 migrations and no later file recreates it (only 20260302200000 and 20260312200000 create it). A `deleted_at`-only UPDATE does not list `status`, so the trigger does not fire at all — the body's status sets (20260706030000:133-138, current definition) are never reached.

3. No `deleted_at`-keyed trigger on quotes exists. `grep -rn "NEW.deleted_at"` returns 16 hits — jobs, blend tickets, returns, invoices, customer documents, commission splits — none on `quotes`. The contrast is decisive: supabase/migrations/20260702174000_layer2_reserve_job_inventory.sql:281 fires the job-hold engine on `NEW.deleted_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.deleted_at`, added precisely because docs/archive/2026-summer-closeout/roadmap/2026-07-01-inventory-aware-scheduling-layer-2-handoff.md:83 says "job soft-delete bypasses status transitions and would orphan holds forever". The same fix was never applied to quotes.

4. The other release paths are closed. `_sync_planned_holds` (latest definition supabase/migrations/20260702171000_layer2_sync_planned_holds_job_aware.sql:41-44) does `WHERE id = p_quote_id AND deleted_at IS NULL FOR UPDATE; IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN 0;`. The cron cleanup `release_expired_quote_holds` (20260302200000_business_logic_enhancements.sql:1515-1535) releases only `WHERE q.status IN ('declined','expired')` — status-based, so it misses a deleted `sent` quote. `auto_expire_quotes` (20260614143649:36) filters `AND q.deleted_at IS NULL`, so the deleted quote never even reaches a terminal status.

5. Readers do not filter deleted quotes. Latest `get_inventory_position` is supabase/migrations/20260716120120_gauntlet_inventory_accuracy.sql:53-62 (supersedes the 20260701203000 version the reviewer cited; the substance is unchanged): `FROM inventory_holds ih WHERE ih.is_active = true AND (ih.expires_at IS NULL OR ih.expires_at >= CURRENT_DATE)` — no join to quotes. Its `planned_quotes` CTE (same file, :80-85) is worse: `JOIN quotes q ON q.id = qi.quote_id WHERE q.is_planned = true AND q.status IN ('draft','sent','revised')` with NO `q.deleted_at IS NULL`, so a soft-deleted planned quote keeps contributing `planned_qty` too. Job shortfall math has the same shape: supabase/migrations/20260710120000_d2_reserve_side_unit_normalization.sql:347-356 `active_holds` sums holds with no quote filter, and :327-331 credits coverage from `ih.source_id = wj.quote_id` regardless of the quote's deleted state.

6. Reachable in production. RLS `quotes_update` (20260206174345:369-377) allows any admin or the owning sales rep to UPDATE quotes directly, and the 20260730235031 hardening revoked direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `quote_sections`/`quote_items` only — `quotes` was deliberately left writable. No detection either: the sentinel's `stale_quote_hold` check (20260705150000_data_integrity_sentinel.sql:212-222) keys on `q.status IN ('declined','expired','cancelled','closed_by_application')`, so a deleted-but-'sent' quote's hold is invisible to it.

7. Not in the named baselines. Neither `hold`, `deleted_at`, nor `soft` appears anywhere in docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md, and docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md has no entry for orphaned holds or Quotes bulk delete. The closest prior art is docs/audits/2026-06-10-error-prevention-execution-log.md:16 — "NEW (found during work): bulk soft-delete hides open bookings with live holds | Quotes.tsx bulk delete skips quotes with draws > 0" — i.e. the draws>0 guard the reviewer quotes IS the historical remedy, and the zero-draw planned-booking residual was never closed. That strengthens the finding rather than refuting it, but the reviewer should cite it.

WHAT IS OVERSTATED (why I cut HIGH to MED):

A. "stay counted forever" is wrong in the common case. `_sync_planned_holds` stamps `expires_at = v_item.needed_by_date + INTERVAL '14 days'` (20260702171000:99), and every reader filters `expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at >= CURRENT_DATE`. The orphan self-heals 14 days past the section's needed-by date. It is indefinite only when `quote_sections.needed_by_date` is NULL — which is possible (nullable: added as `ADD COLUMN ... needed_by_date date` in 20260316500000_planned_programs.sql:6, and absent from the registry's `not_null_columns.quote_sections`, which lists only quote_id/id/section_name/sort_order) — so the unbounded case is a sub-case, not the norm.

B. "nothing in the UI can ever release it" is factually false. src/pages/InventoryPage.tsx:226-237 lists EVERY active, non-expired hold (`.eq('is_active', true).or('expires_at.is.null,expires_at.gte....')`) with no join to quotes — so the orphan is fully visible — and InventoryPage.tsx:447-457 releases it via `release_inventory_hold`, which rejects only `hold_type = 'job'` (supabase/migrations/20260702182000_layer2_release_hold_reject_job.sql:52-55). A crop_program orphan is a one-click admin fix from the Inventory page.

NET: real, unenforced at the DB, reachable by a normal admin action, with no automated detection — but time-bounded in the usual case and admin-recoverable, and it corrupts a planning number rather than money or AR. MED, not HIGH. The correct fix mirrors the jobs pattern: an `AFTER UPDATE OF deleted_at ON quotes` trigger releasing `inventory_holds WHERE source_id = NEW.id`, plus adding `q.deleted_at IS NULL` to the `planned_quotes` CTE in get_inventory_position and extending the sentinel's stale_quote_hold predicate to deleted parents.

confirmed.title: Quotes list Duplicate reuses a stale, page-scoped idempotency key across different quotes — a lost response silently re-opens the previous quote's copy instead of duplicating the one clicked
confirmed.location: src/pages/Quotes.tsx:50, 108-128 (getKey at 111, error return at 117-120, resetKey at 121); supabase/migrations/20260714230000_gauntlet_core_guards.sql:5-51; supabase/migrations/20260526151856_execute_full_codebase_ultra_review.sql (duplicate_quote body)
confirmed.detail:
`duplicateQuoteIdem` is one hook instance for the whole page, and `handleDuplicate` never resets it before the call — it only resets AFTER a successful response (line 121) and returns early without resetting on error (lines 117-120). Every row's Duplicate button shares that one key.

`check_idempotency` is key-only — it compares only `idempotency_key` and `operation`, never the arguments — so a replay for `duplicate_quote` returns the cached result regardless of which `p_source_quote_id` was sent. This is confirmed in the shipped helper, not inferred.

Every sibling handler in this codebase resets per target and this one does not: `openConvert` does `convertQuoteIdem.resetKey()` (Quotes.tsx:137), CommissionPayments resets at each row button (503/526/552), Deliveries resets at modal open (1135-1136), InvoiceDetail resets at 1458, OrderDetail at `onCreateInvoiceClick`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A rep clicks Duplicate on quote Q-1001. The RPC commits (Q-1099 created) but the response is lost to a dropped connection, so the client shows 'Failed to duplicate quote' and the key is NOT reset. The rep scrolls down and clicks Duplicate on a different quote, Q-1042. `duplicate_quote` sees the same key/operation, returns the cached `{quote_id: <Q-1099>, quote_number: 'Q-1099'}`, and the UI toasts 'Quote duplicated as Q-1099' and navigates there. Q-1042 was never duplicated; the rep believes it was, edits Q-1099 (a copy of Q-1001) and sends the wrong products and pricing to the customer.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED on mechanism; severity corrected MED -> LOW. Every factual leg of the claim holds against current source, and I found no missed enforcement anywhere.

(1) Client key lifecycle is as described. `src/hooks/useIdempotencyKey.ts:28-38` scopes the ref to `JSON.stringify([operation, userId])` only — the target row is NOT part of the scope, so one hook instance yields one key for every row. `src/pages/Quotes.tsx:50` declares one page-level `duplicateQuoteIdem`; `handleDuplicate` (108-127) calls `getKey()` at 111 with no pre-reset, returns early at 117-120 on `error` without resetting, and the outer `catch` at 125-127 also does not reset. `resetKey()` at 121 runs only on success. The per-row button at 505 (`onClick={(e) => handleDuplicate(row.id, e)}`) feeds different `quoteId`s into that one key.

(2) The server side is genuinely key-only — this is "the DB does not enforce it", checked in the migrations, not "I couldn't find it". The newest `check_idempotency` is `supabase/migrations/20260714230000_gauntlet_core_guards.sql:5-51`; its lookup is `WHERE idempotency_key = p_key` with only an operation-mismatch raise, no argument/fingerprint comparison. I checked for a superseding definition: the only later files defining it are none — 20260210000000, 20260526201319 (grants only), 20260714220000, then 20260714230000 is last. `duplicate_quote`'s newest definition is `20260526151856_execute_full_codebase_ultra_review.sql:975-1096`; nothing after it redefines the function (grep over all migrations). Its guard at 1006-1010 is `v_existing := check_idempotency(p_idempotency_key,'duplicate_quote'); IF v_existing IS NOT NULL THEN RETURN v_existing; END IF;` — placed BEFORE `SELECT * INTO v_orig FROM quotes WHERE id = p_source_quote_id`, so `p_source_quote_id` is never consulted on replay. The receipt is written in-transaction via `save_idempotency(...)` at 1087, so a committed duplication always leaves a replayable receipt.

(3) I specifically hunted for the enforcement the reviewer might have missed and it does not cover this RPC. The payload-binding mechanism exists — `supabase/migrations/20260803010917_bind_idempotency_to_mutation_intent.sql` adds `idempotency_keys.request_fingerprint` / `request_actor_id` and `IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH` — but it wraps only `save_invoice` and `create_quick_delivery` (grep for IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH: only 20260803010917, 20260806004644, 20260806012423, 20260806023048, all invoice/bulk-import). `duplicate_quote` is listed in `src/lib/rpcIdempotencyScope.test.ts:116` under HELPER_SCOPED, i.e. operation-scoped only — the test contract itself asserts key+operation scoping and nothing more. The BEFORE INSERT trigger `guard_idempotency_key_insert` (20260714230000:65-110) only raises on cross-op reuse or concurrent insert; it never fires on the replay path (the replay returns before any insert).

(4) Not in the baseline. `docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` and `docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md` contain no mention of `duplicate_quote` or a stale duplicate-key; section 04 line 22 only blesses the CONVERT caller. Notably `docs/archive/2026-summer-closeout/build-loops/ui-overhaul-v2/STATE.md:68` records that this exact class ("idempotency-key reuse across different targets on the 3 write buttons") was fixed by adding `resetKey()` on modal-open in Quotes/ReceivingHub/Deliveries — that pass fixed the convert button (`Quotes.tsx:137 convertQuoteIdem.resetKey()`) and left the Duplicate button unfixed, which strengthens rather than refutes the finding.

Two corrections to the finding as written:
- The rhetorical claim "Every sibling handler in this codebase resets per target and this one does not" is inaccurate. `src/pages/CustomerDetail.tsx:1417-1425` ("New from Last") has the identical unreset shape for the same RPC: `getKey()` at 1417, `if (error) { ...; return; }` at 1423, `resetKey()` only at 1425 after success. It is a second instance of the same defect, not a counterexample — but the claimed universal convention does not exist.
- Severity: the failure requires a committed-but-lost response (application errors roll back, so no receipt is left and a stale key is then harmless) AND a subsequent Duplicate on a different row in the same page mount. The blast radius is a silently skipped duplication, not corrupted data: no money, no inventory (the copy is inserted as `'draft'` and `is_planned` is not copied, so no holds are created), and the user is navigated to a quote page showing the other quote's number and customer name. That visible mismatch makes the "sends wrong pricing to the customer" narrative require the rep to ignore a different customer name on the landing page. Real, silent-success-on-a-skipped-write, but LOW rather than MED.

verdict.reason:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED, STATED FAILURE SCENARIO REFUTED. Severity stays LOW.

WHAT VERIFIED CORRECT (all citations exact):
- src/pages/NewDelivery.tsx:116-119 — `.from('orders').select('*, customer:customers(farm_name)').in('status', ['confirmed','partially_fulfilled']).is('deleted_at', null)` (status filter on :118). No `.limit()`/`.range()` anywhere on that query.
- src/pages/NewDelivery.tsx:156-172 — `fetchOrderDetails` is `.from('orders').select('*').eq('id', orderId).maybeSingle()` with NO status filter and NO deleted_at filter. Confirmed.
- src/pages/NewDelivery.tsx:401-403 — `const order = orders.find((o) => o.id === selectedOrderId); if (!order) { toast('error', 'Order not found'); }` searching the FILTERED list. Confirmed.
- Deep-link source exists: src/pages/OrderDetail.tsx:1209 gates the button on `order.status !== 'cancelled' && order.status !== 'fulfilled'`, so a `voided` order does render `navigate('/deliveries/new?order=' + order.id)` at :1213. orders.status enum is ['confirmed','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','voided'] (.claude/schema-registry.json /status_enums/orders.status), so `voided` slips the gate.

WHY THE NARRATED SCENARIO CANNOT HAPPEN (the load-bearing part of the finding is wrong):
A voided order can only have come from `fulfilled` — supabase/migrations/20260616142001_void_order_restore_logs_void_delivery_reversal.sql:55-57 `IF v_order.status != 'fulfilled' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'INVALID_ORDER_STATUS: %'`. And `fulfilled` implies every order_item has quantity_remaining = 0: normal fulfillment only flips to fulfilled when no `quantity_remaining > 0` rows survive, and the only other route (cancel_order remainder-close, supabase/migrations/20260721014858_...govern_invoice_order_money_lifecycle.sql:1140 `quantity_remaining = 0,` → :1247-1248 `'mode','remainder_closed','status','fulfilled'`) explicitly zeroes it. OrderDetail.tsx:625-632 restricts manual transitions to `confirmed:['cancelled'], partially_fulfilled:['cancelled']`, so no manual jump to fulfilled with remaining stock.
Consequence: on a deep link from a voided order, NewDelivery.tsx:207-219 builds `drafts` from `items.filter((item) => item.quantity_remaining > 0)` → EMPTY. The form is NOT "fully populated with pre-filled delivery quantities", and handleSave aborts at NewDelivery.tsx:351-353 with 'Add at least one item with quantity > 0' — line 401 is never reached. The claimed compounding with the voided-order finding does not hold.

WHY IT IS STILL A REAL (LOW) DEFECT — a path the reviewer missed:
Soft-deleted orders reach the same dead end with items populated. Orders.tsx:426 soft-deletes: `supabase.from('orders').update({ deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() }).in('id', ids)`. OrderDetail.tsx:156-159 loads the order with `.select('*').eq('id', id!).maybeSingle()` and NO deleted_at filter, so a soft-deleted `confirmed` order still renders and still shows Schedule Delivery (:1209 gate passes). NewDelivery's list query excludes it via `.is('deleted_at', null)` (:119), but fetchOrderDetails does not, quantity_remaining is still > 0, the form fills in, and save hits the bare 'Order not found'. That is the finding's mechanism, reached by a different door.

ENFORCEMENT CHECK (migrations read, not just "not found"):
The DB DOES enforce order status — supabase/migrations/20260518010000_create_delivery_with_items_validate_order_status_and_address.sql:104-107 `IF v_order.status NOT IN ('confirmed','partially_fulfilled') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'ORDER_NOT_SCHEDULABLE...'`, inside the `SELECT customer_id, status ... FOR UPDATE` at :92-95. I checked every later migration touching the function (20260517010000, 20260530121534, 20260614150249, 20260617013523, 20260620190000) — none redefine it, the last two only mention it in comments. So the status half fails closed twice over.
BUT the RPC does NOT check `deleted_at` on the order (verified by reading the full 20260518010000 body). That makes the frontend `orders.find` guard at :401 load-bearing for the soft-delete case — a "fix" that replaces it with a direct id lookup would open a real hole. This is worth flagging to whoever remediates.

SUB-CLAIM ON PAGINATION: unverified, not refuted. There is genuinely no `.limit()`/`.range()` on the fetchOrders query (I read it), so truncation would depend on the Supabase project's PostgREST max-rows setting, which I cannot check read-only from source. State it as "no client-side limit exists", not as "truncation occurs".

BASELINE: not in docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md and not in docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md — that section's only NewDelivery mention (line 23) is a positive note that delivery creation uses the canonical RPC.

NET: keep the finding at LOW, but the failure_scenario must be rewritten from the voided-order story to the soft-deleted-order story, and the "compounds with the voided-order finding" sentence removed.

This is "the DB does not enforce it," checked against migrations — not "I couldn't find it."
5. No recovery path exists. `auto_expire_quotes()` (supabase/migrations/20260614143649_auto_expire_quotes_skip_planned_and_schedule.sql:33-40) filters `AND q.deleted_at IS NULL ... AND q.is_planned = false` — it skips soft-deleted quotes AND planned quotes, so it never sweeps these. `_sync_planned_holds` (supabase/migrations/20260702171000_layer2_sync_planned_holds_job_aware.sql:41-44) does contain a release arm, but it opens with `SELECT * INTO v_quote FROM quotes WHERE id = p_quote_id AND deleted_at IS NULL FOR UPDATE; IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN 0; END IF;` — it returns early on a deleted quote and never reaches the `UPDATE inventory_holds SET is_active = false` at :50-52. Confirmed no cleanup.
6. Not in either baseline. Neither docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-...md mentions quote soft-delete, stranded holds, or Quote-Hold Parity. Novel.

CORRECTION A — reviewer missed a mechanism (which also misses this case). The reviewer says "the only report that could catch them is structurally unable to." False as stated: a DB-side sentinel exists. `run_data_integrity_sweep()` emits a `stale_quote_hold` alert — newest emit supabase/migrations/20260706030000_closed_short_booking_closure.sql:643-655: `FROM inventory_holds h JOIN quotes q ON q.id = h.source_id WHERE h.is_active = true AND h.hold_type = 'crop_program' AND q.status IN ('declined','expired','cancelled','closed_by_application','closed_short')`. That is exactly the converse check the reviewer says doesn't exist. HOWEVER it keys on terminal STATUS, and a soft-deleted quote keeps status 'sent'/'revised' — and there is no `q.deleted_at IS NOT NULL` arm. So the sentinel misses this precise case too, and the reviewer's conclusion (nothing catches it) stands. The evidence should cite the sentinel and its status-keyed blind spot rather than claiming no converse check exists.

CORRECTION B — the failure scenario is wrong on two counts, and should be restated:
(i) "Net Position keeps that stock reserved forever" is false. `net_position` never subtracts holds: supabase/migrations/20260716120120_gauntlet_inventory_accuracy.sql:169 `(b.quantity_available - b.quantity_prebooked + COALESCE(oo.qty, 0)) AS net_position`, and src/types/index.ts:1007 states it outright — "holds_qty and planned_qty are reported separately; they are NOT subtracted from net_position." The REAL impacts are (a) the displayed reservation, src/pages/InventoryPage.tsx:213 `total_planned_qty: p.holds_qty + p.planned_qty` rendered as the "Planned" column (:143), and (b) an operational block — `create_inventory_hold` computes `v_todays_free := quantity_available - quantity_prebooked - v_active_holds` over ALL active holds and raises `INSUFFICIENT_HOLD_INVENTORY` (supabase/migrations/20260630173022_parked_010_create_inventory_hold_auth_first.sql:170-187), so a phantom hold can refuse a legitimate new reservation.
(ii) "Forever" only holds for undated sections. Planned holds are inserted with `expires_at` = `v_item.needed_by_date + INTERVAL '14 days'` (supabase/migrations/20260702171000_layer2_sync_planned_holds_job_aware.sql:91-99), and every consumer filters `(expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at >= CURRENT_DATE)` — the position RPC's `holds` CTE (20260716120120:59-63) and `create_inventory_hold`'s free calc (20260630173022:174). So a stranded hold on a DATED section ages out of all free/position math 14 days past needed-by (still bounded but potentially many months for a season booking). It is permanent only when `quote_sections.needed_by_date IS NULL` — nullable per supabase/migrations/20260316500000_planned_programs.sql:6 `ALTER TABLE quote_sections ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS needed_by_date date;`, src/types/index.ts:707 `needed_by_date: string | null`, and .claude/schema-registry.json not_null_columns.quote_sections = {no_default: ['quote_id'], with_default: ['id','section_name','sort_order']} — not listed, so nullable live. `NULL + INTERVAL` yields NULL, so those holds never expire out of any filter.

ADJACENT LEAK THE REVIEWER MISSED (same root cause, worth folding in): the position RPC's `planned_quotes` CTE also omits a deleted_at filter — supabase/migrations/20260716120120_gauntlet_inventory_accuracy.sql:81-84 `FROM quote_items qi JOIN quotes q ON q.id = qi.quote_id WHERE q.is_planned = true AND q.status IN ('draft','sent','revised')`. A soft-deleted planned quote keeps that status, so its undrawn booking remainder ALSO keeps inflating `planned_qty` forever — with no expires_at escape hatch at all. That half is strictly worse than the hold half.

SEVERITY: MED sustained. Impact is reporting distortion plus a real `INSUFFICIENT_HOLD_INVENTORY` block on new reservations, with no report or sentinel anywhere that surfaces it; not money, not data loss, and partially self-healing via expires_at. Caveat carried forward: like the reviewer, I read on-disk migrations only — I did not query live pg_proc or live data for existing stranded holds.

confirmed.title: Quote soft-delete writes no activity_feed record — the only quote lifecycle event with no audit trail
confirmed.location: src/pages/Quotes.tsx:406-412 (zero logActivity calls in the whole file); contrast docs/workflows/QUOTE_TO_DELIVERY.md:50 and :252
confirmed.detail: Audited logActivity coverage across the cycle: quote save/send/accept/decline are logged in-transaction by `save_quote` (acknowledged at src/pages/QuoteBuilder.tsx:1541-1542), conversion by `convert_quote_to_order` (2 activity_feed inserts in 20260730235031), the two terminal closures by `close_quote_as_applied`/`close_quote_as_short` (5 activity_feed refs each), payment by `allocate_payment`, invoice post by the `post_invoice` impl chain (20260702160000 body contains `INSERT INTO activity_feed`), unpost by `unpost_invoice`, and order/delivery transitions client-side at OrderDetail.tsx:643 and DeliveryDetail.tsx:904. The one uncovered mutation is quote deletion: `Quotes.tsx` performs a direct table UPDATE setting `deleted_at`, calls no RPC, and the file imports no activity logger at all. Deleting a booking — which by the finding above can also strand inventory — leaves no record of who did it or when.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Five planned bookings vanish from the Quotes list mid-season. There is no activity_feed row, no financial_audit_log row, and no RPC receipt — the only evidence is the `deleted_at` timestamp on the rows themselves, with no actor. Nobody can determine who deleted them or why.

verdict.reason:
CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED, but the framing and half the supporting evidence do not hold up, so severity drops MED -> LOW.

WHAT I INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (all four legs hold):
1. src/pages/Quotes.tsx:406-412 does perform a direct table soft-delete with no RPC: `.from('quotes').update({ deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() }).in('id', ids).select()` followed by `checkMutationResult(result, 'Delete quotes')`. `grep -c logActivity src/pages/Quotes.tsx` -> 0, reproduced.
2. THE DB DOES NOT ENFORCE IT (checked the migrations, not merely "I didn't find it"). I enumerated every trigger on `public.quotes` across all migrations: `enforce_quote_status_transition` (20260228300000:463), `trg_release_holds_on_quote_status` (20260312200000:64), `enforce_quote_accepted_fully_drawn` (20260610181612:293), `trg_enforce_quote_terminal_not_drawn` (20260614151956:51), `trg_validate_quote_commission_split` (20260719064000:142), `quotes_bump_row_version` (20260730235031:64), `trg_stamp_commission_split_recipient_ids` (20260722174029:626). Exactly one writes activity_feed — `release_holds_on_quote_status_change()` — and it is bound `AFTER UPDATE OF status ON quotes` (20260312200000:65-67) with body guard `IF NEW.status IN ('accepted','declined','expired') AND OLD.status NOT IN (...)`. A `deleted_at`-only UPDATE changes no status, so that trigger never fires. No later migration supersedes it with an audit trigger.
3. There is no `deleted_by` column to fall back on. `.claude/schema-registry.json` `columns.quotes` = [... "created_at","updated_at","sent_at","is_planned","season","salesman_id","deleted_at","pdf_template_id","pdf_columns_override","row_version"] — `deleted_at` present, `deleted_by` absent. Contrast src/components/customers/CustomerDocuments.tsx:282 which DOES write `{ deleted_at: ..., deleted_by: deletedBy }`, proving the pattern exists elsewhere in the codebase.
4. Not in either baseline. docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04 covers only the Bulk Order Import HIGH; its sole `activity_feed` mention (line 37) is about `bulk_import_order`. KNOWN_ISSUES.md has only a generic parked LOW bucket ("audit-log completeness gaps", line 935) whose built predicate (line 1032, `predicates/audit-log-completeness.sql`) asserts coverage over "39 money-mutating SECDEF functions" — a direct table write from the Quotes list page is out of that predicate's scope.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG (basis for the downgrade):
a. The title's "the only quote lifecycle event with no audit trail" implies a quote-specific defect. It is the project-wide convention for list-page bulk soft-deletes. Identical unlogged direct `deleted_at` updates: src/pages/Orders.tsx:426 (`grep -c logActivity src/pages/Orders.tsx` -> 0 as well), src/pages/Jobs.tsx:1367, src/pages/BlendTickets.tsx:250, src/pages/BlendRecipes.tsx:296, src/pages/Returns.tsx:599, src/pages/TeamBoard.tsx:455. This is a systemic convention gap, not a quote regression.
b. The cited "contrast" docs do not establish a violated requirement. QUOTE_TO_DELIVERY.md:50 reads "Always call `logActivity()` after send/accept/decline events" and :252 reads "- [ ] Call `logActivity()` for status transitions". A soft-delete is neither — and the code's own comment at Quotes.tsx:378 states "deletion changes no status, so the hold-release trigger never fires". The reviewer's own quoted doc lines therefore do not cover delete.
c. "no financial_audit_log row" is not evidence of anything. Quote deletion moves no money; financial_audit_log is the wrong ledger to expect a row in.
d. The failure scenario overstates "no actor". RLS policy `quotes_update` (supabase/migrations/20260206174345_fix_security_and_performance_issues.sql:369-377) restricts the UPDATE to `is_admin() OR (is_sales_rep() AND created_by = (select auth.uid()))`, with no later policy superseding it. So a non-admin deleter is provably the row's own `created_by`; only an admin deleting another rep's quote is genuinely untraceable. The actor set is bounded, not unknown.
e. Impact is reversible: soft-delete leaves the row and all children intact with `deleted_at` clearable, and `quotes_bump_row_version` (20260730235031:64-67) increments `row_version` on the write, so the mutation is at least detectable. This is an observability gap, not data loss.

VERDICT: real, worth an activity_feed insert or a `deleted_by` column, but it is a reversible, RLS-bounded, no-money observability gap that follows six other pages' existing convention and violates no documented rule. LOW, and properly filed as the systemic "bulk soft-deletes are unaudited" item rather than a quote-lifecycle finding.

4) The 'revised' exclusion is real and reachable. quotes.status in .claude/schema-registry.json is ["draft","sent","revised","accepted","declined","expired","cancelled","closed_by_application","closed_short"]; QuoteBuilder.tsx:1688 `const savedId = await saveQuote('revised')` is the ordinary edit-after-send path, and :455-457 (`canConvert = ['sent','revised','accepted']`, `canDraw = currentStatus === 'sent' || currentStatus === 'revised'`) plus src/lib/openBookings.ts:21 `.in('status', ['sent','revised'])` confirm revised is a live convertible booking that `status IN ('draft','sent')` drops.

6) Not baseline. docs/audits/gauntlet/2026-08-05-section-04-quote-order-delivery-invoice-payment-lifecycle-refresh.md (101 lines, read in full) is entirely about Bulk Order Import and never mentions the dashboard, pipeline value, or revised quotes. docs/manual/KNOWN_ISSUES.md has no entry for financial_dashboard_summary quote aggregation (its "pipeline" hit at :1004 is an unrelated pre-quote sales-pipeline feature note).

One correction to the reviewer's framing, not enough to refute: the identical draft/sent-only, unfiltered-quotes pattern also appears in the sibling operational dashboard — supabase/migrations/20260323100000_operational_dashboard_summary.sql:43-48 `open_quotes AS (SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'draft') AS draft_cnt, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'sent') AS sent_cnt FROM quotes)`, again at :146-151, and at :216-222. So this is a repeated pattern across both dashboard RPCs rather than a one-off slip in one CTE. That widens the defect but weakens the reviewer's rhetorical point that sibling CTEs establish a quote-filtering convention.

Severity LOW is correct and should not be raised: admin-gated (`IF NOT public.is_admin() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'permission denied: admin role required'`), read-only display aggregate, no money movement, nothing stored, no invariant breached. The failure mode is a misleading executive tile, exactly as described.

confirmed.title: AR aging bucket boundaries disagree between the AR Aging report and the Financial Dashboard, and the note saying so lives only in a migration comment
confirmed.detail: get_ar_aging buckets are `<= 29` / `30-59` / `60-89` / `90-119` / `>= 120` (rendered as Current / 30-59 / 60-89 / 90-119 / 120+ at src/pages/ARaging.tsx:231-260). financial_dashboard_summary buckets are `<= 30` / `31-60` / `61-90` / `> 90`. The A8 unification migration explicitly chose not to reconcile them — "The pre-existing bucket-BOUNDARY label differences ... are NOT changed here" — so the divergence is deliberate. Reporting it because the decision is recorded nowhere a reader of either report will find it: not in QUOTE_TO_DELIVERY.md, not in docs/reference/rpc-functions.md:205, not in docs/manual/DECISION_LOG.md, and not on either screen. An invoice exactly 30 days past due appears in "Current" on one page and "30-59 Days" on the other.
confirmed.evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260805151605_fix_historical_ar_report_cutoffs.sql:210-211:
    (COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN p_as_of_date - ei.aging_date <= 29 THEN ei.statement_balance_cents ELSE 0 END), 0)::numeric / 100.0),
